Provincial Regulations

Agricultural Land Commission Act

Agricultural Land Reserve General Regulation

Definitions | Section 1

1   In this regulation:

“Act” means the Agricultural Land Commission Act;

“applicant” includes an agent of the applicant;

“approving officer” means an approving officer or other person described in section 18 (5) [restrictions on approving land uses or subdivision] of the Act;

“local or first nation government applicant” means an applicant who

  1. is a local government or first nation government, and

  2. is making an application with respect to land over which the applicant has jurisdiction;

“public body applicant” means an applicant described in section 16 [public body applicants];

“public hearing” means a public hearing held for the purposes of section 17 (2), 29 (2) or 30 (2) [inclusions or exclusions of land] of the Act, as applicable.

Interpretation | Section 2

2   (1) For the purposes of this regulation,

  1. a local government has jurisdiction over land if the local government has legislative authority over the land, and

  2. a first nation government has jurisdiction over land if the land is, or is part of, the settlement lands or proposed settlement lands, as applicable, for that first nation.

  1. For the purposes of section 2 (1) [application of other Acts] of the Act, nothing in this regulation is to be interpreted as relieving a person from complying with

  1. any other enactment that may apply, or

  2. a decision of a responsible authority, including respecting zoning or subdivision, that may apply.

Subdivision permitted on determination by approving officer | Section 3

3   (1) A subdivision of agricultural land is permitted for the purposes of the Act if

  1. an approving officer determines that the subdivision is of a type referred to in subsection (2), and

  2. the approving officer

  3. indicates the approval by endorsing on the plan of subdivision a certificate in the form required by the commission, and

  1. submits to the commission a copy of the endorsed plan.
  1. The following types of subdivision are permitted for the purposes of subsection (1) (a):

  1. a subdivision that does one or more of the following:

  2. consolidates 2 or more parcels into a single parcel by eliminating common lot lines;

  1. establishes a legal boundary along the boundary of the agricultural land reserve;

Spatial Designation | Designation | 4 - Governance

  1. resolves a building encroachment on a property line, if no additional parcels are created;

  1. a subdivision for which all of the following conditions are met:

  2. the agricultural land to be subdivided involves not more than 4 parcels, each of which is a minimum of 1 ha;

  1. on subdivision, there would be no increase in the number of parcels and no parcel would be less than 1 ha;

  2. the subdivision would allow for boundary adjustments that, in the opinion of the approving officer, will enhance farming on the agricultural land or permit better use of structures used for farming.

Spatial Designation | Licence, Permitting, & Exemptions | 4 - Governance

Subdivision of lands under final agreement permitted | Section 4

4   (1) In this section:

“lands under a final agreement” means those lands affected by a plan that a treaty first nation will own in fee simple, as treaty lands or otherwise, in accordance with the treaty first nation’s final agreement;

“plan” has the same meaning as in section 19 (1) [registration restrictions] of the Act.

  1. A subdivision of agricultural land is permitted for the purposes of the Act if

  1. the subdivision results from the registration of an indefeasible title in the name of a treaty first nation to lands under a final agreement, and

  2. the registration is

  3. effective on the date the final agreement comes into effect, and

  1. in accordance with the final agreement.

Registrar of Titles may accept deposit of permitted plans | Section 5

5   A Registrar of Titles may accept an application for the deposit of a plan referred to in this Part if the applicable conditions of this Part with respect to the subdivision of agricultural land shown on the plan are met.

Applications and application fees | Section 6

6   (1) Subject to subsections (3) and (4) of this section, an applicant may make an application to which section 34 [local government or first nation government review not required] of the Act applies by submitting to the commission

  1. an application in the form and manner required by the commission, and

  2. a fee as follows:

  3. $450 in the case of an application described in section 34 (1) (a), (c) or (e) of the Act that is made for the purposes of section 20.1 (2) (a) of the Act in respect of a non-adhering residential use;

  1. $750 in the case of an application described in section 34 (1) (a), (b), (c) or (e) of the Act other than one that is made for the purposes of section 20.1 (2) (a) of the Act in respect of a non-adhering residential use;

  2. $1 500 in the case of an application made under section 34 (1) (d) of the Act.

  1. Subject to subsections (3) and (4) of this section, an applicant may make an application to which section 34.1 [local government or first nation government review required] of the Act applies by submitting to the applicable body under that section

  1. an application in the form and manner required by the commission, and

  2. a fee as follows:

  3. in the case of an application that is made for the purposes of section 20.1 (2) (a) of the Act in respect of a non-adhering residential use,

  1. $450 for the purposes of section 34.1 (1) of the Act, and

  2. if applicable, an additional $450 for the purposes of section 34.1 (3) of the Act;

  1. in the case of an application other than one that is made for the purposes of section 20.1 (2) (a) of the Act in respect of a non-adhering residential use,

  1. $750 for the purposes of section 34.1 (1) of the Act, and

  2. if applicable, an additional $750 for the purposes of section 34.1 (3) of the Act.

  1. If a fee has already been submitted under section 20.3 (1) (c) (ii) [soil or fill use] of the Act in respect of an application, the fee payable under subsection (1) or (2) (b) (ii) of this section is reduced by $150.

  2. Applicants are exempt from paying application fees in respect of applications to include land in the agricultural land reserve.

Spatial Designation | Licence, Permitting, & Exemptions | 4 - Governance

[am. B.C. Reg. 149/2020, Sch. 1, s. 1.]

Payment by commission for comments or information | Section 7

7   The commission may pay $200 to each local government or first nation government from which the commission requests comments or information under section 34 (3) [local government or first nation government review not required] of the Act.

Local or first nation government review | Section 8

8   (1) A local government or first nation government that receives an application under section 34.1 [application procedure if local government or first nation government review required] of the Act must, in accordance with this section, forward to the commission

  1. the application, and

  2. the comments and recommendations of the local government or first nation government in respect of the application.

  1. The application, comments and recommendations must be forwarded within the following period after the local government or first nation government receives the application:

  1. 90 days, if a public information meeting is held under section 19 (b) [public hearing and public information meeting];

  2. 60 days, if paragraph (a) does not apply.

  1. The comments and recommendations must be in a form acceptable to the commission and address all of the following that apply:

  1. in the case of an exclusion application made by a public body applicant,

  2. whether the notice required under section 17 (a) [exclusion applications by public body applicants] of this regulation has been given,

  1. whether the resolution or law required under section 29 (4) [exclusion applications] of the Act has been made, and

  2. any responses the local government or first nation government received

  1. under section 18 [responses to exclusion applications], and

  2. through a public information meeting held under section 19 (b), if any;

  1. in the case of a use or subdivision application, whether

  2. the resolution, if required under section 25 (3) [applications by owner] of the Act, has been made, or

  1. the law required under section 25 (3.1) of the Act has been made.
  1. The comments and recommendations may include any other information the local government or first nation government wants the commission to consider concerning the application.

Procedures at meetings and public hearings | Section 9

9   (1) The commission, a local government, a first nation government or a public body applicant that holds a meeting, public information meeting or a public hearing with respect to an application may, without limiting any other powers of the commission, local government, first nation government or public body applicant,

  1. designate the date, time and place for the meeting or public hearing, and

  2. adjourn the meeting or public hearing.

  1. The commission, a local government, a first nation government or a public body applicant holding a public hearing

  1. must give all persons present an opportunity to be heard on matters related to the proposal or application that is the subject of the public hearing, and

  2. may, without further notice, allow a proposal or application that is the subject of the public hearing to be amended to accommodate representations made at that public hearing.

  1. A member of the commission, a local government or a first nation government who was not present at a public hearing may vote on the proposal or application that was the subject of the public hearing if an oral or written report of the public hearing has been given to the member.

Notice of action | Section 10

10   (1) Without limiting any other requirement under the Act, the commission must give written notice to each applicable person referred to in subsection (2) if the commission does any of the following, whether on the commission’s own initiative or on determination of an application:

  1. includes, or refuses to include, land in the agricultural land reserve;

Spatial Designation | 4 - Governance

  1. excludes, or refuses to exclude, agricultural land from the agricultural land reserve;

Spatial Designation | 4 - Governance

  1. grants, or refuses to grant, permission for a use or subdivision;

  2. reverses or varies a decision on reconsideration under the Act.

  1. The persons who must receive notice are the following:

  1. the applicant;

  2. the local government or first nation government that has jurisdiction over the land that is the subject of the action.

Fees if action of official required | Section 11

11   (1) An applicant must pay a fee in accordance with this section if

  1. the commission, on granting an application, imposes a term or condition on the applicant, and

  2. the effect of the term or condition is to cause an official to engage in an activity described in this section.

  1. At the time that the term or condition is imposed, an applicant must pay a fee as follows:

  1. $350 for each site inspection an official must conduct, unless subsection (3) applies;

  2. $150 for each of the following that an official must administer, process, prepare, review, execute, file or register, other than in the context of an application:

  3. a contract or similar legal instrument, report, survey, map or a form of security;

  1. a record that must be approved, filed or registered under an enactment;

  2. a plan within the meaning of section 19 [registration restrictions] of the Act or a covenant, including related records necessary for deposit of the plan or covenant with a Registrar of Titles.

  1. On the annual date set by the commission, an applicant must pay a fee as follows for each year or part of a year that an official monitors activities conducted on agricultural land:

  1. $500 for agricultural land surveyed as being less than 0.8 ha;

  2. $1 000 for agricultural land surveyed as being between 0.8 ha and 4 ha;

  3. $2 000 for agricultural land surveyed as being more than 4 ha.

Publishing the status of applications | Section 12

12   (1) The commission must publish the following information in respect of each application:

  1. the date on which the application was received;

  2. in general terms, the intent of the application;

  3. the name of the applicant;

  4. the dates on which the commission began and completed its review of the application;

  5. the commission’s determination and the reasons for it.

  1. For the purposes of subsection (1),

  1. publication must be on a website maintained by or on behalf of the commission, and

  2. published information must be kept current.

Proposals by commission | Section 13

13   If the commission is proposing on the commission’s own initiative to include land in, or exclude agricultural land from, the agricultural land reserve, the commission must do all of the following:

Spatial Designation | Instruction | 4 - Governance

  1. give notice of the proposal not less than 3 days and not more than 10 days before the date of the public hearing;

  2. give a copy of the proposal and supporting material to each local government or first nation government whose interests, the commission believes, will be affected by the application;

  3. post a sign, in a form and manner acceptable to the commission, on the land that is the subject of the application.

Applications by local or first nation government applicants | Section 14

14   (1) If a local or first nation government applicant is applying to include land in, or exclude agricultural land from, the agricultural land reserve, the applicant must do all of the following:

Spatial Designation | Instruction | 4 - Governance

  1. give notice of the application not less than 3 days and not more than 10 days before the date of the public hearing;

  2. give a copy of the application to the following:

  3. if the land that is the subject of the application is adjacent to an area over which a different local government or first nation government has jurisdiction, that different local government or first nation government;

  1. each local government or first nation government whose interests, the local or first nation government applicant believes, will be affected by the application;

  2. include with the application

  3. a report of the public hearing and any additional public comments, and

  4. any other supporting material the commission may require;

  5. post a sign, in a form and manner acceptable to the commission, on the land that is the subject of the application.

  1. Despite subsection (1) (b), a local or first nation government applicant is not required to give a copy of an application to a first nation government referred to in paragraph (b) of the definition of “first nation government” in section 1 of the Act.

Notice of public hearing | Section 15

15   (1) A notice of a public hearing must be given in accordance with this section by

  1. the commission, in respect of a proposal on the commissions’ own initiative to include land in, or exclude agricultural land from, the agricultural land reserve, and

Spatial Designation | 4 - Governance

  1. a local or first nation government applicant, in respect of an application by the applicant to include land in, or exclude agricultural land from, the agricultural land reserve.

Spatial Designation | Administration, Application, & Structure | 4 - Governance

  1. The notice must do all of the following:

  1. state the general intent of the proposal or application;

  2. identify the land affected, whether by using the legal description or by describing the land generally;

  3. state the date, time and place of the public hearing;

  4. state when and where a copy of the proposal or application may be inspected.

  1. The notice must be published as follows:

  1. publication must be in at least 2 issues of a newspaper within the meaning of the Community Charter;

  2. the newspaper must be circulated in the municipality, regional district or settlement lands within which the land that is the subject of the proposal or application is located;

  3. the last publication must be circulated not less than 3 days and not more than 10 days before the date of the public hearing.

  1. Despite subsection (3) of this section, if the requirements of that subsection are not practical, the commission or local or first nation government applicant, as applicable, may give notice in the same manner as a council may give notice under section 94 (4) and (5) of the Community Charter.

Exclusion applications by public body applicants | Section 17

17   If a public body applicant is applying to exclude agricultural land from the agricultural land reserve, the public body applicant must do all of the following:

Responses to exclusion applications | Section 18

18   (1) If a public body applicant receives a response to a notice given under section 17 (a) [exclusion applications by public body applicants], the applicant must promptly forward the response to the local government or first nation government that has jurisdiction over the agricultural land that is the subject of the application.

  1. A local government or first nation government that receives a copy of an application under section 17 (b) may respond to the application by giving comments and recommendations to the local government or first nation government that has jurisdiction over the agricultural land that is the subject of the application.

Public hearing and public information meeting | Section 19

Commission meeting | Section 20

20   (1) The commission must do all of the following:

  1. hold a meeting to determine an exclusion application;

  2. not more than 30 days before the meeting, give written notice of the meeting to

  3. the applicant,

  1. the local government or first nation government that has jurisdiction over the agricultural land that is the subject of the application, and

  1. hear representations from the applicant;

Evidence presented at meeting | Section 21

21   (1) This section applies if

  1. evidence is presented at a meeting of the commission held to determine an exclusion application, and

  2. a statement or summary of that evidence has not been given to the applicant before the meeting.

  1. If the applicant is present at the meeting, the commission may

  1. hear further representations in respect of the evidence, or

  2. adjourn the meeting to enable the applicant to answer the evidence.

  1. If the applicant is not present at the meeting, the commission must notify the applicant personally or by registered or electronic mail of

  1. the evidence, and

  2. the date by which the additional evidence may be answered.

Transportation and utility use applications | Section 22

22   (1) For the purposes of section 34 (1) (d) [local government or first nation government review not required] of the Act, an application for any of the following uses must, unless the use is permitted under the Agricultural Land Reserve Use Regulation, be filed directly with the commission:

Definition | Section 24

24   In sections 25 [residency information] and 26 [determining residency in administrative region], “director” means the director of the office of the government that is responsible for the recruitment and recommendation of candidates for appointments to all Crown corporations, agencies, boards and commissions.

Residency information | Section 25

25   (1) A person is a resident of an administrative region if the person

  1. is a citizen or permanent resident of Canada,

  2. resides in the administrative region, and

  3. intends to return to the administrative region when absent.

  1. A person seeking to be appointed as a member of the commission must do all of the following:

  1. identify to the director, in writing,

  2. the administrative region of which the person is a resident, and

  1. either the regional district in which the person is a resident or, if the person resides in the area referred to in section 4 (b) of the Schedule to the Act, that area;
  1. provide supporting evidence for the purpose of subsection (1).
  1. The director may request additional supporting evidence to that provided under subsection (2) (b).

Determining residency in administrative region | Section 26

26   (1) If the director is satisfied that a person seeking to be appointed as a member of the commission is a resident of the administrative region identified by the person under section 25 (2) (a) (i) [residency information], the director must provide confirmation of that fact and the information provided under that section to

  1. the Lieutenant Governor in Council, in the case of a person seeking to be appointed as chair of the commission, and

  2. the minister, in any other case of a person seeking to be appointed as a member of the commission.

  1. Confirmation by the director that a person is a resident of an administrative region must be in writing and is final and binding.

Mapping of agricultural land reserve boundaries | Section 27

27   The commission must ensure that

  1. the agricultural land reserve boundary is represented on maps using technology, standards and security procedures the commission considers appropriate, and

Reports to minister | Section 28

28   The commission must submit to the minister reports as follows:

  1. before June 30 of each year, an annual report that includes information respecting the financial operation of the commission and a financial statement

  2. showing the commission’s financial operations for the 2 preceding financial years, and

  1. prepared in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles and the accounting policies and practices established by Treasury Board;

  1. on request of the minister, a report that includes the following information with respect to the period specified by the minister:

  2. information specified by the minister respecting the administration of the Act by the commission and the expenditure of the budget allocated to the commission;

  1. information respecting expenditures in relation to specific budget allocations.

Publishing reports | Section 29

29   (1) Subject to subsection (2) of this section, the commission must publish on a website maintained by or on behalf of the commission a report submitted under

  1. section 44 [report and recommendations respecting matters referred to the board] of the Act, and

  2. section 28 [reports to minister] of this regulation, no earlier than 60 days and not later than 90 days after submitting the report.

  1. The minister may direct the commission not to publish any part of a report that, in the opinion of the minister, contains information that would be protected from disclosure under Division 2 of Part 2 of the Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act, whether the information relates to the commission or to the government.

Penalties for contraventions | Section 30

30   (1) The chief executive officer must consider all of the following before levying a penalty against a person for contravening the Act, the regulations or an order of the commission:

  1. the gravity and magnitude of the contravention;

  2. whether the contravention was deliberate, repeated or continuous;

  3. whether there has been any contravention of a similar nature by the person;

  4. whether the person derived an economic benefit from the contravention;

  5. the person’s cooperativeness and efforts to correct the contravention;

  6. the degree to which the contravention detrimentally affected or impaired the agricultural capability of agricultural land or its suitability for farming.

  1. The maximum penalty which the chief executive officer may levy is as follows:

  1. for any single contravention, $100 000;

  2. for a subsequent contravention, double the amount of the penalty levied for the first contravention.

Notice of action | Section 31

31   (1) In this section, “action” means a determination or an order made, or a penalty levied, under section 50 [stop work order], 52 [determinations and remediation orders] or 54 (1) [penalties levied by chief executive officer] of the Act.

  1. An official who takes an action must give notice of the action to the person against whom it is taken.

  2. If the chief executive officer levies a penalty against a person for contravening the Act, the regulations or an order of the commission, the chief executive officer must set out all of the following in the notice:

  1. the nature of the contravention;

  2. the amount of the penalty;

  3. the date by which the penalty must be paid;

  4. a description of the person’s right to appeal the penalty.

Giving a notice of action | Section 32

32   (1) An official who is required to give notice under section 31 (2) [notice of action] must give the notice by one or more of the following means:

  1. personally;

  2. by registered mail sent to the person’s last known address;

  3. by electronic mail sent to the person’s last known electronic mail address;

  4. by posting the notice at a conspicuous location on the agricultural land that is the subject of the notice.

  1. Notice is deemed to have been received by the person who is the subject of the notice as follows:

  1. if sent in accordance with subsection (1) (b), on the 14th day after deposit with Canada Post unless the person actually received the notice before that day;

  2. if sent in accordance with subsection (1) (c), as follows:

  3. as provided for under section 18 (2) of the Electronic Transactions Act;

  1. despite subparagraph (i), no later than 96 hours after the notice was sent.

Service and receipt of notice and records generally | Section 33

33   Except as otherwise set out in this regulation,

  1. if the commission is required to give a notice under the Act, the commission may determine the form and manner of giving the notice, and

  2. if a person other than the commission is required to give a notice under the Act, the person must do so in a form and manner acceptable to the commission.

Notice of statutory right of way | Section 34

34   (1) For the purposes of section 18.1 (3) [notice of statutory right of way] of the Act, the form issued by the commission to the applicant under subsection (2) of this section, confirming that the commission received notice in accordance with section 18.1 (2) of the Act, is proof that notice has been given as required under that section.

  1. The commission

  1. must, if it received notice in accordance with section 18.1 (2) of the Act, issue a form confirming that fact, and

  2. may issue the form electronically or otherwise.

[am. B.C. Reg. 149/2020, Sch. 1, s. 3.]

Fee if notice of intent to remove soil or place fill | Section 35

35   A person who submits to the chief executive officer a notice of intent to remove soil or place fill on agricultural land must pay a fee of $150.

Delegation to British Columbia Energy Regulator | Section 36

36   The commissioner appointed under the Energy Resource Activities Act is prescribed as a public officer for the purposes of section 26 (1) (b) [delegation of powers respecting applications] of the Agricultural Land Commission Act.

[am. B.C. Reg. 187/2023, Sch., s. 12.]

Agricultural Land Reserve Use Regulation

Definitions | Section 1

1   In this regulation:

“Act” means the Agricultural Land Commission Act;

“agri-tourism activity” means an activity referred to in section 12 [agri-tourism];

“compost” means a product that is

  1. a stabilized earthy matter having the properties and structure of humus,

  2. beneficial to plant growth when used as a soil amendment,

  3. produced by composting, and

  4. derived only from organic matter;

“controlled environment structure” means a structure that provides a controlled environment intended to intensify crop production, including, without limitation,

Spatial Designation | Prohibition, Restriction, or Limitation | 4 - Governance

  1. a vertical farming system,

  2. a rotating tray system, or

  3. any other structure that minimizes the use of land, controls the use of light, air, water or nutrients or relies in whole or in part on automation,

but not including

  1. a greenhouse,

  2. a structure for mushroom production, or

  3. a structure described in section 8 (1) (b) or (2) that is used for producing cannabis in accordance with section 8;

“farm product” means a commodity that is produced from a farm use but does not include water;

“gathering for an event” means a gathering of people on agricultural land for the purpose of attending

  1. a wedding, other than a wedding to which paragraph (c) (ii) applies,

  2. a music festival, or

  3. an event, other than

13   (1) In this section:

“alcohol product” means beer, cider, spirits, mead or wine;

“ancillary use” means the following activities conducted at an alcohol production facility:

  1. processing, storing and retail sales of an alcohol product produced by the alcohol production facility;

  2. operating a food and beverage service lounge, if the area of the lounge does not exceed 125 m2 indoors and 125 m2 outdoors;

  3. selling an alcoholic beverage other than one produced by the alcohol production facility, if the alcoholic beverage is intended to be consumed immediately and is sold

  4. as a single serving in a lounge referred to in paragraph (b), or

  1. gathering for an event, if the event is held only in the lounge referred to in paragraph (b) or the special event area under a special event area endorsement referred to in paragraph (c), and, for this purpose, section 17 [gathering for an event] does not apply;

“brewery”, “cidery”, “distillery”, “meadery” and “winery” mean a brewery, cidery, distillery, meadery or winery, as applicable, that is licensed under the Liquor Control and Licensing Act to produce beer, cider, spirits, mead or wine;

“primary farm product” means the farm product that is the primary ingredient used in a fermentation process to make an alcohol product.

  1. The use of agricultural land for constructing, maintaining and operating an alcohol production facility and the use of the facility for ancillary uses are designated as farm uses and may not be prohibited as described in section 4 if

  1. at least 50% of the primary farm product used to make the alcohol product produced each year is harvested from the agricultural land on which the alcohol production facility is located, or

  2. the agricultural land on which the alcohol production facility is located is more than 2 ha in area and at least 50% of the primary farm product used to make the alcohol product produced each year is

  3. harvested from that agricultural land, or

  1. both harvested from that agricultural land and received from a farm operation located in British Columbia that provides that primary farm product to the alcohol production facility under a contract having a term of at least 3 years.

Definitions | Section 1

1   (1) In this regulation:

“accredited zoo or aquarium” means a zoo or an aquarium that

  1. is accredited by Canada’s Accredited Zoos and Aquariums, or

  2. provides proof to the satisfaction of the director of meeting or exceeding the accreditation standards set by Canada’s Accredited Zoos and Aquariums;

“Act” means the Wildlife Act;

Species Status and Assessment | Interpretation & Purpose | 4 - Governance

“aquatic invasive species individual” means a single live member of a controlled alien species designated in Schedule 3 or 4, at any developmental stage;

Invasive Species and Disease | 8.1 Invasive Non-Native / Alien Species | Interpretation & Purpose | 3 - Habitat

“BC waters” includes

  1. any part of a body of water that is located in British Columbia,

  2. fish habitat as defined in the Water Sustainability Regulation,

Water Use and Watercourse Modifications | 7.2 Dams & Water Management / Use | 3 - Habitat

  1. a stream as defined in the Water Sustainability Act,

Water Use and Watercourse Modifications | 7.2 Dams & Water Management / Use | 3 - Habitat

  1. a ditch, and

  2. any of the following that may leak, drain or empty, directly or indirectly, into any part of a body of water, fish habitat, stream or ditch referred to in paragraph (a), (b), (c) or (d):

Water Use and Watercourse Modifications | 7.2 Dams & Water Management / Use | Authorization & Mandate | 3 - Habitat

  1. a naturally-formed pool of water other than one referred to in paragraph (a), (b), (c) or (d);

  2. a storm drain, sewer or other artificial conduit;

  3. a tank or other container that holds or is intended to hold water or wastewater;

“certified educational institution” means a body that

  1. is an educational body within the meaning of paragraph (a), (c), (d) or (d.1) of Schedule 1 of the Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act, and

  2. holds a valid Certificate of Good Animal Practice issued by the Canadian Council on Animal Care;

“certified research institution” means a body that

Human Disturbance | 6.3 Other Human Disturbances | Interpretation & Purpose | 3 - Habitat

  1. holds a valid Certificate of Good Animal Practice issued by the Canadian Council on Animal Care, and

“mussel” means a single member, live or dead, of a controlled alien species designated in Schedule 4, and if live, at any developmental stage;

Invasive Species and Disease | 8.1 Invasive Non-Native / Alien Species | Interpretation & Purpose | 3 - Habitat

“prohibited species individual” means any of the following:

  1. a single live member of a controlled alien species designated in Schedule 1, at any developmental stage;

  2. a single live member of a controlled alien species designated in section 1 (1) or (2) of Schedule 2 that is 3 metres or more in length when measured from the front of the snout to the tip of the tail while the animal is fully extended;

  3. a single live member of a controlled alien species designated in section 1 (3) of Schedule 2 that is 2 metres or more in length when measured from the front of the snout to the tip of the tail while the animal is fully extended;

“release” includes, for the purpose of applying section 7 (3) of this regulation and section 77 (2) of the Act to a mussel, allowing the mussel to come into contact with BC waters;

Invasive Species and Disease | 8.1 Invasive Non-Native / Alien Species | Interpretation & Purpose | 3 - Habitat

“restricted species individual” means a single live member of a controlled alien species designated in Schedule 2, at any developmental stage, but does not include a prohibited species individual.

Preventing entry or spread of mussels | Section 9

9   (1) In this section:

“boat or water equipment” means any of the following items:

  1. a boat, including personal watercraft;

  2. a boat trailer;

  3. any item used for fishing;

Fisheries | 5.4 Fishing, Harvesting & Controlling Aquatic Species | 2 - Fish

  1. any item used for water-based recreational activities;

  2. any equipment associated with, and any component of, a thing referred to in any of paragraphs (a) to (d);

“contaminated province or state” means any of the following:

  1. a jurisdiction listed in Schedule 5;

Species Status and Assessment | 4 - Governance

  1. a province or territory of Canada or a state of the United States of America that is not listed in Schedule 5 but has within its jurisdiction one or more bodies of water that are contaminated with mussels;

Species Status and Assessment | 4 - Governance

“decontamination order” means an order issued by an officer under subsection (3).

  1. An officer may issue a decontamination order in respect of a boat or water equipment if any of the following circumstances exist:

  1. the officer has visually inspected the boat or water equipment and found signs that that boat or water equipment may be or may have been contaminated with mussels;

  2. the boat or water equipment is owned, or is registered, licensed, insured or otherwise authorized to be possessed or operated, in a contaminated province or state;

  3. the officer has reason to believe that the boat or water equipment has been operated in, or has otherwise come into contact with, the waters of a contaminated province or state;

  4. the officer has reason to believe that a person may be in violation of section 7 of this regulation or any of sections 33 (2), 37 or 77 (2) of the Act with respect to mussels.

  1. An officer may issue a decontamination order requiring a person to do one or more of the following:

  1. remove mussels from a boat or water equipment within a reasonable period of time as specified in the order;

  2. comply with any written directions contained in or attached to the order with respect to the removal of mussels;

  3. report, within the time and to the officer specified in the order,

  4. with proof, satisfactory to the specified officer, of compliance with the order, or

  1. for the purposes of further inspection by the specified officer of the boat or water equipment that is the subject of the order.
  1. A person to whom a decontamination order is issued must

  1. comply with the order, and

  2. ensure that the boat or water equipment to which the order applies does not come into contact with BC waters until the order has been complied with.

  1. A person who engages in procedures to remove mussels from a boat or water equipment must ensure that water used in those procedures does not come into contact with BC waters.

  2. For the purposes of subsection (3) (c), an officer may be specified by name or by class.

[en. B.C. Reg. 402/2012, s. 8; am. B.C. Reg. 48/2014, s. 5.]

1.01.01   For the purposes of section 51 (1) (a) (iii) of the Wildlife Act, a regional manager may not issue a guide outfitter licence to a person unless the person is 19 years of age or older.

Species Status and Assessment | Licence, Permitting, & Exemptions | 4 - Governance

[en. B.C. Reg. 1/2019, Sch. 4, s. 1.]

Public liability insurance | Section 1.01.1

1.01.1   (1) For the purposes of section 51 (1) (a) (ii) of the Wildlife Act, a regional manager may issue a guide outfitter licence to a person if the person has public liability insurance as follows:

Species Status and Assessment | Licence, Permitting, & Exemptions | 4 - Governance

  1. the amount of the insurance must be at least $2 million;

  2. the insurance must be applicable to the guide outfitter’s guiding business;

  3. the insurance must cover the guiding activities of each assistant guide employed by the guide outfitter as permitted under section 48 (1.1) of the Wildlife Act.

Species Status and Assessment | Licence, Permitting, & Exemptions | 4 - Governance

  1. A guide outfitter must continue to have public liability insurance as described in subsection (1) while the guide outfitter is licensed.

[en. B.C. Reg. 1/2019, Sch. 4, s. 2.]

Delivery of guide report | Section 1.05.1

1.05.1   (0.1) In this section, “guide report” means a guide report referred to in section 55 (1) of the Wildlife Act.

Species Status and Assessment | Interpretation & Purpose | 4 - Governance

  1. A guide outfitter must do one of the following within 30 days after a hunt is concluded:

  1. submit to the regional manager the original of the completed guide report that relates to the hunt;

  2. submit to the regional manager, in the form and manner specified by the director, the information in the completed guide report that relates to the hunt.

  1. A guide outfitter who contravenes subsection (1) commits an offence.

[en. B.C. Reg. 67/2012, s. (b); am. B.C. Regs. 230/2019, Sch. 3; 112/2021, App. 4, s. 1.]

Reports relating to grizzly bears | Section 2.01.1

2.01.1   (1) A taxidermist or tanner who receives a grizzly bear or a part of a grizzly bear must submit a report to the director within 10 days after receipt of the bear or part.

  1. A report under subsection (1) must include

  1. the information set out in section 2.01 (1) (a) to (d), and

  2. if the bear or part is acquired from an individual, the address of the primary residence of the individual.

  1. A person who contravenes subsection (1) commits an offence.

[en. B.C. Reg. 52/2018, Sch. 4, s. 3.]

Term of five year trapping licence | Section 2.04.1

2.04.1   A five year trapping licence is valid from and including the later of

  1. July 1 of the year in which it is issued, or

  2. the date on which it is issued

to June 30 of the year 5 years after the year in which the licence was issued.

[en. B.C. Reg. 238/2007, s. (d).]

Compulsory report of fur bearing animals killed | Section 3.16.1

3.16.1   (1) In this section:

“FWID number” has the same meaning as in the Wildlife Act General Regulation;

Species Status and Assessment | 4 - Governance

“trapping year” means the period beginning July 1 and ending June 30.

  1. A person who holds a trapping licence issued under section 40.1 of the Wildlife Act must submit a report to the director, in accordance with this section, respecting fur bearing animals killed under the licence during the trapping year.

Species Status and Assessment | Licence, Permitting, & Exemptions | 4 - Governance

  1. The report must include the person’s trapping licence number and FWID number.

  2. If the person did not kill a fur bearing animal under the licence during the trapping year, the report must

  1. state that no fur bearing animals were killed, and

  2. be submitted on or before July 31 of the following trapping year.

  1. If the person killed one or more fur bearing animals under the licence during the trapping year, the report must include all of the following information for each fur bearing animal killed:
  1. the management unit in which the fur bearing animal was killed and either

Spatial Designation | 4 - Governance

  1. the trapline number, or

  2. a statement that the kill occurred on private property;

  1. the month in which the fur bearing animal was killed;

  2. the fur bearing animal’s species and sex.

  1. The information required under subsection (5)

  1. may be submitted, with respect to one or more fur bearing animals killed during the trapping year, at any time during the trapping year, and

  2. must be submitted, with respect to all fur bearing animals killed during the trapping year, on or before July 31 of the following trapping year.

  1. For greater certainty, the reporting requirements under this section are in addition to those imposed under section 3.16.

  2. A person commits an offence if the person fails to make a report as required under this section with respect to

  1. the trapping year that begins July 1, 2022, and

  2. each subsequent trapping year.

[en. B.C. Reg. 167/2021, App. s. 2.]

Transporter licence reporting requirement | Section 5.05.1

5.05.1   (1) A holder of a transporter licence must file in accordance with subsection (2) a completed licence activity report setting out the information required by the form of that report in relation to the holder’s transporting activities for the year.

  1. A licence activity report must be filed

  1. with the regional manager indicated on the transporter licence, and

  2. by December 31 of each year.

  1. A holder of a transporter licence who fails to file a licence activity report in accordance with this section commits an offence.

[en. B.C. Reg. 1/2019, Sch. 4, s. 10.]

Definitions | Section 1.01

1.01   In this Division:

“permanent identification number” means a unique number assigned under the authority of the director to a person who passes an assistant guide examination approved or established by the director;

“written authorization” means an authorization issued by a guide outfitter to an assistant guide.

[en. B.C. Reg. 18/2015, Sch. 1, s. 1 (b).]

Offence | Section 1.02

1.02   Where a guide outfitter guides, the guide outfitter commits an offence unless, at the time the guide outfitter

  1. guides, or

  2. employs an assistant guide to guide on the guide outfitter’s behalf,

the guide outfitter is insured under a policy of public liability insurance as described in section 1.01.1.

[am. B.C. Regs. 217/2000, s. 1; 18/2015, Sch. 1, s. 2; 74/2017, App. 5, s. 2.]

  4. the number of hunters or a class of hunters that may hunt a species in a defined time and area.

[am. B.C. Reg. 74/2017, App. 5, s. 3.]

1.041   (1) It is a term and condition of every guide outfitter licence that the holder must not block or damage a road, trail, airstrip or watercourse or other real or personal property while providing services under a guide outfitter licence.

  1. Without limiting section 16.01 (i) of the Wildlife Act General Regulation, a holder of a guide outfitter licence who contravenes the term and condition referred to in subsection (1) of this section commits an offence.

Offence | Section 1.05

1.05   (1) A guide outfitter or assistant guide commits an offence if, while guiding for big game, the guide outfitter or assistant guide

  1. guides more than 2 hunters at one time, or

  2. fails to accompany a hunter the guide outfitter or assistant guide is guiding.

  1. A guide outfitter commits an offence if the guide outfitter

  1. guides a hunter outside the guide outfitter’s guiding area, or

  2. allows an assistant guide employed by the guide outfitter to guide a hunter outside the guide outfitter’s guiding area.

  1. An assistant guide employed by a guide outfitter commits an offence if the assistant guide guides a hunter outside the guide outfitter’s guiding area.

  2. An offence under subsection (2) or (3) of this section is prescribed as an offence for the purposes of section 84 (1) (b) (ii) of the Wildlife Act.

Written authorizations | Section 1.17

1.17   For the purposes of section 48 (1.2) of the Wildlife Act, the written authorization that a guide outfitter issues to an assistant guide must be legible and contain the following information:

Species Status and Assessment | Instruction | 4 - Governance

  1. the name, birth date and permanent address of the assistant guide;

  2. the permanent identification number of the assistant guide;

  3. the name of the guide outfitter;

  4. the number of the guide outfitter’s licence;

  5. the date the written authorization is issued;

  6. the date the term of the guide outfitter’s licence ends;

  7. the statement: “(name of assistant guide) has been hired as an assistant guide.”;

  8. any restrictions on the assistant guide when guiding for game on behalf of the guide outfitter contained in the contract between the guide outfitter and the assistant guide, such as restrictions relating to seasons, areas or species;

  9. a signed statement by the guide outfitter that, to the best of the guide outfitter’s knowledge, the information contained in the written authorization is true, accurate and complete.

Bear parts prohibitions — general | Section 2.08

2.08   (1) A person commits an offence by possessing any of the following parts of a bear:

  1. a gall bladder or bile;

  2. male genitalia separated from the carcass and the hide.

  1. Despite subsection (1), a person who possesses a gall bladder or bile of a bear does not commit an offence under subsection (1) (a) if

  1. the gall bladder is attached to the carcass,

  2. the bile has not been extracted from the gall bladder, and

  3. the person killed the bear no more than 48 hours previously and has not yet gutted the bear.

(2.1) An offence under subsection (1) of this section is prescribed as an offence for the purposes of section 84 (1) (b) (ii) of the Wildlife Act.

Interpretation | Section 3.01

“compound crossbow” means a crossbow on which the bow string passes through a series of pulleys;

“egg trap” means a holding device set in a manner designed to capture a raccoon by a front paw;

“foot snare” means a snare that is set in a manner designed to capture an animal by the foot or leg;

“foot-hold trap” means a trap or device, other than a snare, that is set in a manner designed to capture the animal for which it is set by the foot or leg;

“killing snare” means a snare that is set in a manner designed to capture an animal by the neck;

“killing trap” means a trap or trapset that is designed to kill an animal;

“management unit” or “M.U.” means an area designated as a management unit by B.C. Reg. 64/96, the Management Unit Regulation;

Spatial Designation | Interpretation & Purpose | 4 - Governance

“modified foot-hold trap” means a trap that has

  1. a minimum space of 5 mm between the jaws of the trap when in a closed position,

  2. manufactured pads of a rubber-like substance fastened to the trap jaws, or

  3. lamination of the trap jaws to increase the surface area of the jaw face;

“Region 1” means the area within M.U.s 1-1 to 1-15;

“Region 2” means the area within M.U.s 2-1 to 2-19;

“Region 3” means the area within M.U.s 3-12 to 3-20 and 3-26 to 3-46;

“Region 4” means the area within M.U.s 4-1 to 4-9 and 4-14 to 4-40;

“Region 5” means the area within M.U.s 5-1 to 5-15;

“Region 6” means the area within M.U.s 6-1 to 6-30;

“Region 7” means the area within M.U.s 7-1 to 7-58;

“Region 8” means the area within M.U.s 8-1 to 8-15 and 8-21 to 8-26;

“trapping” means the act of setting or placing a trap in an operative condition or killing by the use of a firearm.

Examination of traplines | Section 3.05

3.05   (1) A holder of a licence, permit or other authorization to trap commits an offence by failing to examine

  1. every 72 hours, every holding or non-killing trap, except an egg trap, set by that licence holder,

  2. every 24 hours, every egg trap set by that licence holder, and

  3. every 14 days, every killing trap or killing snare set by that licence holder.

  1. A holder of a licence, permit or other authorization to trap on private property commits an offence unless the person examines the holding or non-killing traps the person has set on private property at least once every 24 hours.

[en. B.C. Reg. 454/82; am. B.C. Regs. 273/84, s. 5; 254/92, s. 5; 193/2002, s. 1; 74/2017, App. 5, s. 4.]

3.06   A person who traps within 200 m of a dwelling commits an offence unless the person is using,

  1. if the trap is set on land, a live box trap or egg trap, or

  2. if the trap is set on or in water,

  3. a Conibear trap not larger than size No. 330, or equivalent,

  1. foot-hold traps not larger than size No. 2, or

  2. submarine traps.

  2. Despite subsection (1), there is no open season on white or blue (glacier) coloured black bears.

  1. the person

  2. in effect at the time of the application for a transporter licence, and

Transporting Application

Management Plan Form

The Management Plan Form, when completed, describes the proposed operation of an applicant for a transporter licence. The purpose of this form is to:

• obtain information detailing an applicant’s proposed operation,

• act as a resource document to be used by the ministry to evaluate and adjudicate applications for transporter licences, and

• provide the basis for transporter licence conditions.

If a transporter licence is issued on the basis of the information provided in this form, the completed form becomes part of the transporter licence documentation and the director may use the information to set terms and conditions in the transporter licence. Failure of the licence holder or the licence holder’s employees to comply with licence conditions may lead to administrative action or prosecution.

For further information or assistance regarding the completion of this form, please contact the nearest regional office of the Ministry of Environment.

[en. B.C. Reg. 340/2005, s. 15; am. B.C. Regs. 159/2008, s. 3; 138/2013, s. (b); 64/2021, s. 3.]

Definition | Section 12.01

12.01   In this Division, “main portion” means,

  1. in relation to big game, the edible meat of the four quarters, loins, neck and ribs, and

  2. in relation to a game bird, the edible meat of both breasts.

[en. B.C. Reg. 52/2018, Sch. 5, s. 1.]

Exemption — small game | Section 12.02

12.02   A person who hunts and kills small game, other than a game bird or a fur bearing animal, is exempt from section 35 (2) (b) of the Act in relation to the game killed.

[en. B.C. Reg. 52/2018, Sch. 5, s. 1.]

Exemption — game taken for hide | Section 12.03

12.03   A person who hunts and kills game that is a fur bearing animal other than a black bear and removes the hide to any of the following is exempt from section 35 (2) (b) of the Act in relation to the game killed:

  1. a dwelling place of the person;

  2. a taxidermist, tanner, fur trader or the owner or operator of a cold storage plant.

[en. B.C. Reg. 52/2018, Sch. 5, s. 1.]

Exemption — game taken for food | Section 12.04

12.04   A person who hunts and kills a game bird or big game and makes every reasonable effort to remove the main portions to any of the following is exempt from section 35 (2) (b) of the Act in relation to the game killed:

  1. the person’s normal dwelling place;

  2. a meatcutter or the owner or operator of a cold storage plant.

[en. B.C. Reg. 52/2018, Sch. 5, s. 1.]

Exemption — transfers of game | Section 12.05

12.05   A person who hunts and kills game and transfers the game killed to another person is exempt from section 35 (2) (b) of the Act in relation to the game killed if

  1. the game is a fur bearing animal other than a black bear and the other person removes the hide to a dwelling place of the other person or to a person described in section 12.03 (b) of this regulation, or

  2. the other person makes every reasonable effort to remove the edible portions or, in the case of a game bird or big game, the main portions to the other person’s normal dwelling place or to a person described in section 12.04 (b) of this regulation.

[en. B.C. Reg. 52/2018, Sch. 5, s. 1.]

Minimum hunting age | Section 15.01

15.01   (1) A person under the age of 10 years may not hunt wildlife.

Proof of identity | Section 21.01

21.01   (1) For the purposes of section 97 (2) (b) and (4) (b) of the Act, the following photo identification is prescribed:

  1. in the case of a person who is a resident or a non-resident, valid photo identification issued to the person by any of the following:

  2. the government of Canada;

  1. the government of a province or territory, or an agent of the government of a province or territory, in which the person has a current address;

  2. the Nisg̱a’a Nation, if the person is a Nisg̱a’a citizen;

  3. a treaty first nation, if the person is a treaty first nation member of the treaty first nation;

  1. in the case of a person who is a non-resident alien,

  2. valid photo identification in the form of

  1. a passport, or

  2. a driver’s licence issued to the person by a foreign jurisdiction in which the person has a current address, or

  1. a copy of a photo identification referred to in subparagraph (i) that has been certified as a true copy by

  1. a lawyer, or

  2. a notary who is a member in good standing under the Notaries Act;

  1. in any case, a valid NEXUS card.
  1. For the purposes of section 97 (5) of the Act, persons under 16 years of age are prescribed as exempt from the requirement to produce photo identification.

[en. B.C. Reg. 127/2017, App. 8, s. 2; am. B.C. Regs. 79/2018, App. 4, s. 2; 85/2019, Sch. 2, s. 1; 230/2019, Sch. 4; 42/2020.]

Proof of authorization | Section 21.02

21.02   (1) For the purposes of section 97 (3) (b) (ii) of the Act, a person who holds any of the following authorizations may demonstrate that the person holds the authorization by stating the person’s FWID number:

  1. a hunting licence;

  2. a special area licence required by Part 2 or 3 of the Hunting Licensing Regulation, B.C. Reg. 8/99;

  3. a limited entry hunting authorization;

  4. a guide outfitter licence;

  5. an upland game bird licence;

  6. a permit issued under section 70 (1) (a) of the Act.

  1. For the purposes of section 97 (3) (b) of the Act, a person who is required to produce a species licence must produce an original species licence.

[en. B.C. Reg. 127/2017, App. 8, s. 2; am. B.C. Regs. 127/2017, App. 12; 55/2018; 85/2019, Sch. 2, s. 1.]

21.03   (1) A person described in section 11 (1.1) of the Act who hunts must, on the request of an officer,

  1. state the person’s name and address,

  2. produce photo identification referred to in section 21.01 (1) of this regulation, and

  3. demonstrate that a hunting licence is held on the person’s behalf by

  4. producing the hunting licence or a legible copy of the hunting licence, or

  1. stating the person’s FWID number.
  1. Subsection (1) (b) does not apply to a person under 16 years of age.

[en. B.C. Reg. 127/2017, App. 8, s. 2; am. B.C. Reg. 85/2019, Sch. 2, ss. 1 and 2.]

How to give notice | Section 22.02

22.02   A notice to which this Division applies must be given to a person in one of the following methods:

  1. by leaving a copy with the person;

  2. by sending a copy by ordinary mail or registered mail to the last known address of the person or, if the person carries on a business, to the address at which the person carries on business;

  3. by leaving a copy in a mailbox or mail slot for the last known address of the person or, if the person carries on a business, for the address at which the person carries on business;

  4. by attaching a copy to a door or other conspicuous place at the last known address of the person or, if the person carries on a business, at the address at which the person carries on business;

  5. by fax to a number, or by email to an email address, provided by the person;

  6. by sending a copy to an online account held by the person on a website that

  7. is maintained by or on behalf of the minister, and

  1. immediately sends an email notification to an email address provided by that person.

[en. B.C. Reg. 85/2019, Sch. 2, s. 3.]

When notice must be considered received | Section 22.03

22.03   A notice given in accordance with section 22.02 is deemed to be received as follows:

  1. if given by sending a copy by ordinary mail or registered mail, the 14th day after it is mailed;

  2. if given by leaving a copy in a mailbox or mail slot, the 3rd day after it is left;

  3. if given by attaching a copy to a door or other conspicuous place, the 3rd day after it is attached;

  4. if faxed or emailed, the 3rd day after it is sent;

  5. if given by sending a copy to an online account on a website that also sends an email notification, the 3rd day after it is sent to the account.

[en. B.C. Reg. 85/2019, Sch. 2, s. 3.]

“bait” means anything, including meat, cereal, cultivated crops, a restrained animal or any manufactured product or material, that may attract wildlife, but does not include a decoy;

Animal Health Act

Animal Products and Byproducts Regulation

Definitions | Section 1

1   In this regulation:

“Act” means the Animal Health Act;

Aquaculture and Hatcheries | 2.4 Marine & Freshwater Aquaculture | Interpretation & Purpose | 2 - Fish

“bee” has the same meaning as in the Bee Regulation, B.C. Reg. 3/2015;

“cappings” has the same meaning as in the Bee Regulation, B.C. Reg. 3/2015;

“comb” has the same meaning as in the Bee Regulation, B.C. Reg. 3/2015;

“farmed bird” means a chicken, Cornish hen, duck, emu, goose, ostrich, partridge, pheasant, pigeon, quail, squab or turkey hatched or raised on a farm;

“fur bearing animal” has the same meaning as in the Fur Farm Regulation, B.C. Reg. 8/2015;

“game” has the same meaning as in the Game Farm Regulation, B.C. Reg. 5/2015;

“hide” has the same meaning as in the Livestock Licensing Regulation, B.C. Reg. 6/2015;

“livestock” has the same meaning as in the Livestock Licensing Regulation, B.C. Reg. 6/2015.

From bees | Section 2

2   (1) The following are prescribed as animal products from bees for the purposes of the Act and the regulations made under it:

  1. honey;

  2. pollen.

  1. The following are prescribed as animal byproducts from bees for the purposes of the Act and the regulations made under it:

  1. beeswax;

  2. cappings;

  3. combs;

  4. propolis;

  5. a queen cell, being a wax comb cell that contains a developing queen bee that is near to emerging.

From farmed birds | Section 3

3   (1) Eggs from farmed birds are prescribed as animal products for the purposes of the Act and the regulations made under it.

  1. Feathers from farmed birds are prescribed as animal byproducts for the purposes of the Act and the regulations made under it.

From fish and shellfish | Section 4

4   (1) The following are prescribed as animal products from finfish for the purposes of the Act and the regulations made under it:

Aquaculture and Hatcheries | 2.4 Marine & Freshwater Aquaculture | Designation | 2 - Fish

  1. eggs;

  2. oil.

  1. The following are prescribed as animal byproducts for the purposes of the Act and the regulations made under it:
  1. fish meal made from finfish;

Aquaculture and Hatcheries | 2.4 Marine & Freshwater Aquaculture | 2 - Fish

  1. fertilizers and hydrolysates made from finfish;

Aquaculture and Hatcheries | 2.4 Marine & Freshwater Aquaculture | 2 - Fish

  1. shells from crustaceans or molluscs.

From mammals | Section 5

5   (1) Milk from livestock or water buffalo, including butter, cream, cheese and other dairy products made from that milk, is prescribed as an animal product for the purposes of the Act and the regulations made under it.

Aquaculture and Hatcheries | 2.4 Marine & Freshwater Aquaculture | Designation | 2 - Fish

  1. The following are prescribed as animal byproducts for the purposes of the Act and the regulations made under it:

  1. blood, bones, bristle, hair, hides, hooves, horns and offal from livestock or water buffalo;

  2. antlers from game;

  3. wool from sheep;

  4. pelts from fur bearing animals.

From any animal | Section 6

6   (1) Meat from farmed birds, finfish, crustaceans, molluscs, livestock or water buffalo is prescribed as an animal product for the purposes of the Act and the regulations made under it.

Aquaculture and Hatcheries | 2.4 Marine & Freshwater Aquaculture | Designation | 2 - Fish

  1. Non-fertilized ova and semen from farmed birds, finfish, crustaceans, molluscs, livestock, water buffalo or fur bearing animals are prescribed as animal byproducts for the purposes of the Act and the regulations made under it.

Aquaculture and Hatcheries | 2.4 Marine & Freshwater Aquaculture | Designation | 2 - Fish

  5. Apis vilutina [Asian predatory wasp];

  6. Tropilaelaps clareae [Asian bee mites];

  7. Vespa mandarinia [Asian giant hornet].

  1. Illness in bees caused by American foulbrood is prescribed as a reportable disease.

In Appendix 1 and 2, if a reference to a disease or infestation is followed by italicized text in square brackets that is or purports to be descriptive of the disease or infestation, the italicized text in square brackets is not part of this regulation and is to be considered to have been added editorially for convenience of reference.

Invasive Species and Disease | 8.4 Pathogens | 2 - Fish

Bird diseases | Section 2

2   (1) The following are prescribed as reportable diseases in respect of birds:

  1. Fowl typhoid caused by Salmonella gallinarum;

  2. any strain of H5 or H7 avian influenza A virus;

Invasive Species and Disease | 8.4 Pathogens | 2 - Fish

  1. Infectious laryngotracheitis;

  2. Mycoplasma gallisepticum, but only in turkeys kept or dealt with for commercial purposes;

  3. Newcastle disease;

Invasive Species and Disease | 8.4 Pathogens | 2 - Fish

  1. Pullorum diseases caused by Salmonella pullorum.
  1. Avian influenza A viruses other than strains of H5 or H7 are prescribed as reportable diseases in respect of birds if there is

  1. a positive influenza A matrix PCR result, and

  2. high flock morbidity showing severe clinical signs, including any of the following:

  3. signs of respiratory distress;

  1. swelling of the sinuses or head;

  2. reduced vocalization;

  3. a marked reduction in food or water intake;

  4. cyanosis of the unfeathered skin, wattles and comb;

  5. uncoordinated or nervous behaviour;

  6. diarrhea;

  7. a marked drop in egg production;

  8. a high and rapidly escalating flock mortality.

2   The following are prescribed as notifiable diseases in respect of birds:

  1. Avian chlamydiosis caused by Chlamydophila psittaci;

  2. Influenza A in poultry, other than as described in section 1 (1) (b) or (2) of Appendix 1;

  3. Fowl cholera caused by Pasteurella multocida;

  4. Fowl pox.

Records and samples | Section 3

3   (1) A person who makes a report under section 20 [mandatory reporting] of the Act must keep the following in relation to the report:

  1. a record of the matters described in section 20 (3) (a) to (e) of the Act, for at least 30 days after making the report;

  2. all records within the person’s possession or control that are relevant to information requested under section 20 (3) (g) of the Act, for at least 30 days after making the report;

Fisheries | 5.4 Fishing, Harvesting & Controlling Aquatic Species | 2 - Fish

  1. all samples taken for the purpose of making a diagnosis of a reportable or notifiable disease, or unusual illness, for at least 7 days after making the report.

Invasive Species and Disease | 8.4 Pathogens | Interpretation & Purpose | 2 - Fish

  1. A person who makes a report under section 20 of the Act must

  1. keep and produce records in accordance with section 19 [duty to keep records] of the Act, and

  2. provide to the chief veterinarian, on request of the chief veterinarian and within the time requested, a sample referred to in subsection (1) (c) of this section.

  1. Despite subsection (1), the chief veterinarian may request a person to keep a record or sample referred to in that subsection for a longer period, and the person must comply with that request.

Cattle diseases | Section 3

3   The following are prescribed as reportable diseases in respect of cattle:

  1. Bovine cysticercosis;

  2. Bovine spongiform encephalopathy;

  3. Bovine tuberculosis caused by Mycobacterium bovis;

  4. Contagious bovine pleuropneumonia;

  5. Lumpy skin disease.

Invasive Species and Disease | 8.4 Pathogens | 2 - Fish

3   The following are prescribed as notifiable diseases in respect of cattle:

  1. Bovine trichomoniasis;

  2. Bovine genital campylabacteriosis.

Making reports | Section 4

4   (1) The chief veterinarian may

  1. establish forms for the purposes of making a report under section 6 (2) [must comply with veterinary advice], 20 [mandatory reporting] or 21 [mandatory diagnostic examination and reporting] of the Act, and

  2. issue instructions respecting the manner in which a report may be made.

  1. A person who must make a report under section 6 (2), 20 or 21 of the Act must use all applicable forms established, and comply with all applicable instructions issued, under subsection (1) of this section.

  2. A person must make a report as follows:

  1. for the purposes of section 6 (2) of the Act, within 24 hours of becoming aware of the non-compliance with instructions given under section 6 (1) of the Act;

  2. for the purposes of section 20 of the Act, within 24 hours of becoming aware of the applicable matter described in section 20 (2) of the Act;

  3. for the purposes of section 21 of the Act, within the time set out in the order issued under section 21 (1) of the Act.

  1. If the chief veterinarian permits a report to be sent by courier or regular mail, the report is deemed to have been made on the date stamped on the envelope by Canada Post or another delivery agent.

Invasive Species and Disease | 8.4 Pathogens | Designation | 2 - Fish

  1. the illness has never, or has rarely been, observed in British Columbia;

Invasive Species and Disease | 8.4 Pathogens | 2 - Fish

  1. the illness has, or appears to have, a higher pathogenicity than usual.
  1. An illness in any animal is prescribed as a reportable disease if clusters of the illness include more animals, appear more frequently, or appear over a larger geographic area than usual.

Antisapstain Chemical Waste Control Regulation

Interpretation | Section 1

1   (1) In this regulation:

“antisapstain chemical” means chlorophenol, 2-(thiocyanomethylthio) benzothiazole (TCMTB), copper-8-quinolinolate (Cu-8), 3-iodo-2-propynyl butyl carbamate (IPBC) and didecyldimethyl ammonium chloride (DDAC);

Pollution | 9.1 Water-Borne & Other Effluent Pollution | Interpretation & Purpose | 3 - Habitat

“chlorophenol” means the sum of chlorophenols plus chlorophenates as reported by a laboratory testing method approved by a director;

“curb” means a raised edge or curbing which would confine all liquids dropping within the enclosure formed by it and the surface on which it sits;

“effluent” includes precipitation runoff;

Pollution | 9.1 Water-Borne & Other Effluent Pollution | 3 - Habitat

“fixed roof” means a roof which is designed and constructed to prevent the entry of precipitation and to be a maintenance free structure for a period of not less than 10 years, but does not include a structure which utilizes tarpaulins or similar materials;

“impervious” means not allowing entrance or passage of antisapstain chemicals;

“isolated” means set apart from other operations in an enclosure away from any high traffic areas that can, under normal circumstances, prevent the entry of unauthorized persons.

  1. For the purposes of this regulation effluent is toxic if the effluent at 100% concentration kills 50% or more of rainbow trout within 96 hours when tested in accordance with procedures approved by a director.

unless the person

Interpretation — specified industrial or commercial uses | Section 1.1

1.1   For the purposes of the definition of “specified industrial or commercial use” in section 39 (1) of the Act, the purposes and activities set out in Schedule 2 of this regulation are prescribed as industrial and commercial purposes or activities.

[en. B.C. Reg. 161/2020, App. 2, s. 2.]

Interpretation — high and low density residential land uses | Section 1.2

1.2   For the purposes of the definitions of “high density land use” and “low density land use” in section 1, a land use that would otherwise be a high density residential land use is to be considered to be a low density residential use if the land is also used

Spatial Designation | Interpretation & Purpose | 4 - Governance

  1. to grow plants for human consumption, or

  2. as a playground, sports field, picnic area or other use that involves frequent contact with the soil by children.

[en. B.C. Reg. 133/2022, App., s. 1 (c).]

Interpretation — decommissioning a site | Section 2.1

2.1   For the purposes of section 40 (2) (a) (i) of the Act and this Part, an owner or operator decommissions a site if the owner or operator does any of the following in a manner designed to stop all specified industrial or commercial uses of the site:

  1. removes or treats soil;

  2. removes, destroys or treats buildings or process equipment, including storage tanks.

[en. B.C. Reg. 161/2020, App. 2, s. 3.]

Interpretation — ceasing operations at a site | Section 2.2

2.2   For the purposes of section 40 (2) (a) (ii) of the Act and this Part, an owner or operator ceases operations on land if

  1. the owner or operator ceases using the land for a specified industrial or commercial use, and

  2. the land is not used for any specified industrial or commercial uses for 12 months after the date on which the specified industrial or commercial use referred to in paragraph (a) ceases.

[en. B.C. Reg. 161/2020, App. 2, s. 3.]

Site disclosure statements by persons applying to approving officers or municipalities | Section 3

3   A person who is required to provide a site disclosure statement under section 40 (1) of the Act must provide the site disclosure statement at the time of presenting, in writing, an application or request for approval described in that section.

[en. B.C. Reg. 131/2020, App., s. 3.]

Site disclosure statements by municipalities undertaking zoning or rezoning | Section 3.1

3.1   A municipality that, under section 40 (1) (b) (i) of the Act, is undertaking to zone or rezone land in which it has an ownership interest must provide a site disclosure statement to the registrar within 15 days after giving first reading to the applicable zoning bylaw.

[en. B.C. Reg. 131/2020, App., s. 3.]

Site disclosure statements by owners or operators of land | Section 3.2

3.2   (1) A person who is required to provide a site disclosure statement under section 40 (2) (a) of the Act in relation to land must provide the site disclosure statement to the registrar within 6 months after the owner or operator

  1. decommissions a site on the land, or

  2. ceases operations on the land.

  1. A person who is required to provide a site disclosure statement under section 40 (2) (b) of the Act must provide the site disclosure statement within 90 days after filing for protection under, or otherwise becoming subject to, the Companies’ Creditors Arrangement Act (Canada).

  2. A person who is required to provide a site disclosure statement under section 40 (2) (c) of the Act must provide the site disclosure statement within 90 days after filing a proposal, or a notice of intention to make a proposal, under Part III of the Bankruptcy and Insolvency Act (Canada).

[en. B.C. Reg. 131/2020, App., s. 3.]

Site disclosure statements by vendors of real property | Section 3.3

3.3   A vendor of real property who is required to provide a site disclosure statement under section 40 (6) of the Act must provide the site disclosure statement as follows:

  1. unless paragraph (b) applies, at least 30 days before the actual transfer of the real property;

  2. if the time between the written agreement for the transfer of the real property and the actual transfer is less than 30 days, before the written agreement is entered into.

[en. B.C. Reg. 131/2020, App., s. 3.]

Site disclosure statements by persons who take possession or control of real property | Section 3.4

3.4   A person who is required to provide a site disclosure statement under section 40 (7) of the Act must provide the site disclosure statement to the registrar within 10 days after the person takes possession or control of real property referred to in that provision.

[en. B.C. Reg. 131/2020, App., s. 3.]

Request for information by municipality or approving officer | Section 3.5

3.5   Nothing in this Part restricts the authority of a municipality or approving officer to request a person applying for or otherwise seeking approval of a matter referred to in section 40 (1) of the Act to provide the information required by a site disclosure statement even though the person is not required under the Act to provide a site disclosure statement.

[en. B.C. Reg. 131/2020, App., s. 3.]

Exemption — other processes apply under the Act | Section 4

4   (1) A person is exempt from the requirement to provide a site disclosure statement under section 40 (1) or (2) of the Act in relation to a site if

  1. the site is the subject of an approval in principle or certificate of compliance relevant to

  2. the current use of the site, or

  1. any use of the site proposed by the person, and
  1. the person, after making reasonable inquiries, has no reason to believe that any further contamination occurred at the site after the approval in principle or certificate was issued.
  1. A person is exempt from the requirement to provide a site disclosure statement under section 40 (1) or (2) of the Act in relation to a site if
  1. the site is located within an environmental management area for which a director has approved

  1. a wide area remediation plan, or

  1. the site disclosure statement would be provided only as a result of uses or activities that caused contamination that is dealt with in the approved plan or scope.
  1. A person is exempt from the requirement to provide a site disclosure statement under section 40 (1) or (2) of the Act in relation to a site if

  1. a determination was made under section 44 of the Act that the site is not a contaminated site, and

  2. the person, after making reasonable inquiries, has no reason to believe that any contamination occurred at the site after the determination was made.

[en. B.C. Reg. 161/2020, App. 2, s. 3.]

Exemption — persons applying to approving officers | Section 4.1

4.1   (1) A person is exempt from the requirement to provide a site disclosure statement to an approving officer under section 40 (1) (a) of the Act if either of the following applies:

  1. the person is an applicant for subdivision under section 114 of the Land Title Act;

  2. the proposed subdivision consists only of

  3. an adjustment to the boundary of a parcel, or

[en. B.C. Reg. 161/2020, App. 2, s. 3.]

Exemption — persons applying to municipalities | Section 4.2

4.2   (1) A person is exempt from the requirement to provide a site disclosure statement to a municipality under section 40 (1) (b) (i) of the Act if

  1. the land in relation to which the person is seeking approval for zoning is being used for a specified industrial or commercial use, and

  2. the specified industrial or commercial use would continue to be authorized on the land if the zoning were approved.

(1.1) A person is exempt from the requirement to provide a site disclosure statement to a municipality under section 40 (1) (b) (ii) of the Act if the land is the site of a waste management facility that is
