  2. the equipment is capable of maintaining temperatures necessary to comply with section 40 (1) [temperature standards];

  3. the equipment is equipped with a device to measure temperature that is accurate to within 1°C.

  1. A seafood processor must ensure that the temperature inside refrigeration equipment in the seafood processor’s licensed facility is measured and recorded at least once in each 24 hour period.

Protection of food | Section 38

38   A seafood processor must ensure that the seafood processor’s licensed facility is operated, and activities carried out under the licence are conducted, in a manner that will prevent fish and aquatic plants from becoming unsafe food.

Food safety plans | Section 39

39   (1) In this section:

“critical control point” means a procedural step, when carrying out activities under a licence, at which an action can be taken to prevent, eliminate, or reduce to an acceptable level, the risk of fish and aquatic plants becoming unsafe food;

“critical limit” means a threshold, limit or standard that must be met at a critical control point to ensure that fish and aquatic plants do not become unsafe food.

Fisheries | 5.4 Fishing, Harvesting & Controlling Aquatic Species | Prohibition, Restriction, or Limitation | 2 - Fish

  1. A seafood processor must do all of the following:

  1. develop and maintain a food safety plan in accordance with subsection (3);

  2. ensure that the food safety plan is implemented in the seafood processor’s licensed facility;

  3. keep records respecting

  4. the results of monitoring and verification activities under the food safety plan, and

  1. the corrective actions that have been taken when critical limits have not been met;

  2. keep the food safety plan in a conspicuous location in the seafood processor’s licensed facility;

  1. make the food safety plan and the records referred to in paragraph (c) available to an inspector on request;

  2. review the food safety plan, and change it if necessary,

  3. at least annually, and

  1. if any significant change is made to the construction or operation of the seafood processor’s licensed facility.
  1. A food safety plan must be in writing and must identify all of the following:

  1. those hazards that may cause fish and aquatic plants to become unsafe food, and the measures needed to address those hazards;

  2. the process and information used for the purpose of identifying the hazards and measures under paragraph (a);

  3. based on the hazard analysis under paragraph (a), all critical control points and, for each critical control point,

  4. the critical limit, and

Fisheries | 5.4 Fishing, Harvesting & Controlling Aquatic Species | Prohibition, Restriction, or Limitation | 2 - Fish

  1. procedures to monitor the critical control point and to determine whether the critical limit has been met;

Fisheries | 5.4 Fishing, Harvesting & Controlling Aquatic Species | Prohibition, Restriction, or Limitation | 2 - Fish

  1. if a critical limit has not been met, corrective actions that must be taken to meet the critical limit or eliminate unsafe food;

Fisheries | 5.4 Fishing, Harvesting & Controlling Aquatic Species | Prohibition, Restriction, or Limitation | 2 - Fish

  1. verification procedures, including procedures, tests, sampling and other evaluative methods, to be taken to ensure that monitoring procedures under paragraph (c) (ii) and corrective actions under paragraph (d) are being carried out as intended;

  2. the form of the records that must be kept under subsection (2) (c).

  1. A seafood processor must change the seafood processor’s food safety plan in accordance with the directions of an inspector.

Temperature, water and ice standards | Section 40

40   (1) A seafood processor must ensure that fish in the seafood processor’s licensed facility are maintained as follows:

  1. in the case of live fish, at a temperature and in other conditions suitable to the species of fish;

Fisheries | 5.4 Fishing, Harvesting & Controlling Aquatic Species | 2 - Fish

  1. in the case of fresh fish, at a temperature of no less than 0°C and no more than 4°C;

  2. in the case of frozen fish, at a temperature of -18°C or less.

Fisheries | 5.4 Fishing, Harvesting & Controlling Aquatic Species | 2 - Fish

  1. A seafood processor must ensure that water and ice used in the seafood processor’s licensed facility for the purpose of carrying out activities under the licence is of adequate quality to prevent fish and aquatic plants from becoming unsafe food.

Sanitation plans | Section 41

41   (1) A seafood processor must do all of the following with respect to the seafood processor’s licensed facility:

  1. develop and maintain a sanitation plan in accordance with subsection (2);

  2. ensure that the sanitation plan is implemented;

  3. keep records respecting activities carried out for the purpose of implementing the sanitation plan;

  4. make the sanitation plan and the records referred to in paragraph (c) available to an inspector on request.

  1. A sanitation plan must be in writing and must identify all of the following:

  1. the cleaning and sanitizing requirements, with respect to the licensed facility and all equipment used in the licensed facility, necessary to keep fish and aquatic plants from becoming unsafe food;

  2. the cleaning and sanitizing agents, and pesticides, used in the licensed facility, including their concentrations, uses and storage requirements.

  1. A seafood processor must change the seafood processor’s sanitation plan in accordance with the directions of an inspector.

Sanitation | Section 42

42   A seafood processor must ensure that the seafood processor’s licensed facility and the equipment used in the licensed facility are maintained in a condition that will prevent fish and aquatic plants from becoming unsafe food, including ensuring that

  1. equipment is regularly sanitized, with food contact surfaces kept as free as possible of disease-causing micro-organisms, and

Invasive Species and Disease | 8.4 Pathogens | 2 - Fish

  1. pest-proof containers for the disposal of refuse are readily accessible.

Invasive Species and Disease | 8.1 Invasive Non-Native / Alien Species | 3 - Habitat

Pollution | 9.1 Water-Borne & Other Effluent Pollution | 3 - Habitat

Hygiene | Section 43

43   (1) A seafood processor must ensure that employees, while in the seafood processor’s licensed facility,

  1. wear clothing, footwear and coverings on their hands that is clean and appropriate to the activity in which employees are engaged,

  2. exhibit cleanliness and good personal hygiene, and

  3. do not engage in any activity that may cause fish and aquatic plants to become unsafe food.

  1. A seafood processor must ensure that employees wash their hands as often as necessary to prevent fish and aquatic plants from becoming unsafe food.

  2. A seafood processor must ensure that persons do not use tobacco or vapour products, within the meaning of the Tobacco and Vapour Products Control Act, in any area of the licensee’s licensed facility where fish or aquatic plants are processed, stored or distributed.

Illnesses | Section 44

44   A seafood processor must not permit a person suspected to suffer from, or be the carrier of, an illness communicable through food to come into contact with any fish, aquatic plants or equipment in the licensee’s licensed facility.

Fisheries | 5.4 Fishing, Harvesting & Controlling Aquatic Species | Prohibition, Restriction, or Limitation | 2 - Fish

Animals | Section 45

45   A seafood processor must ensure that live animals are not in or on the seafood processor’s licensed facility, except as follows:

  1. a guide dog or a service dog within the meaning of the Guide Dog and Service Dog Act is permitted, except in any area in which fish or aquatic plants are processed or stored;

  2. live fish may be kept as permitted by an inspector.

Fisheries | 5.4 Fishing, Harvesting & Controlling Aquatic Species | Licence, Permitting, & Exemptions | 2 - Fish

Storage of chemicals | Section 46

46   A seafood processor must ensure that chemicals, cleansers and similar agents are stored in the seafood processor’s licensed facility

  1. in a manner that cannot cause fish and aquatic plants to become unsafe food, and

  2. in containers that are clearly labelled to identify the contents.

Storage of packaging, ingredients and additives | Section 47

47   (1) A seafood processor must ensure that the following items, if stored in the seafood processor’s licensed facility, are stored only in dedicated areas in the licensed facility:

  1. items to be used as packaging, including labels;

  2. ingredients and additives used in processing.

  1. A seafood processor must ensure that items, ingredients and additives referred to in subsection (1) are each

  1. stored in a manner that will protect them from conditions that may cause them to become damaged or altered in a manner that may cause fish and aquatic plants to become unsafe food, and

  2. clearly identified with a label.

Storage of inedible products and fish offal | Section 48

48   A seafood processor must ensure that unsafe food, fish offal and byproducts are stored in containers that are

  1. kept separate from fish, aquatic plants and products that may be distributed for human consumption, and

  2. are clearly labelled as being unfit for human consumption.

No storage of unnecessary items | Section 49

49   A seafood processor must ensure that items that are not required for the carrying out of activities under the licence are not stored in or on the seafood processor’s licensed facility.

Prohibitions on processing | Section 50

50   (1) A seafood processor must not process fish or aquatic plants unless the fish or aquatic plants are received by the seafood processor from one of the following sources:

  1. a person who holds a licence under this regulation with respect to the fish or aquatic plant, as applicable;

  2. a person who holds a licence or other authorization under a provincial food enactment;

  3. subject to subsection (2), a person who holds a federal licence to conduct activities in relation to food for public consumption;

  4. a person having lawful authority to harvest the fish or aquatic plant.

  1. A seafood processor must not receive for processing cultured fish raised by marine aquaculture unless the cultured fish have been previously processed or held by a person holding a federal licence to process cultured fish.

Aquaculture and Hatcheries | 2.4 Marine & Freshwater Aquaculture | Prohibition, Restriction, or Limitation | 2 - Fish

Processing lobsters and crab | Section 51

51   A seafood processor must not process any lobster or crab that is dead before processing begins, unless the lobster or crab is being further processed after previous processing.

Federal canning regulations apply | Section 52

52   (1) This section applies despite section 3 of the Fish Inspection Regulations (Canada).

  1. A seafood processor must comply with all applicable requirements and prohibitions of the following provisions of the Fish Inspection Regulations (Canada) as if the seafood processor was a registered establishment within the meaning of that regulation:

  1. section 34;

  2. section 35;

  3. section 37;

  4. section 38 (1);

  5. section 39 (1);

  6. section 40 (1);

  7. section 42;

  8. sections 47 to 50.

  1. For the purposes of section 49 of the Fish Inspection Regulations (Canada), the requirements of section 25 of that regulation also apply.

Processing bivalve molluscs | Section 53

53   (1) A seafood processor must not receive bivalve molluscs for processing unless

  1. the bivalve molluscs have been previously processed or held by a person holding a federal licence to process bivalve molluscs, and

  2. the processed bivalve molluscs are in containers that are tagged according to the requirements of the Canadian Shellfish Sanitation Program Manual of Operations, made under section 15 (8) (c) of the Fish Inspection Regulations (Canada).

  1. A seafood processor must ensure that shucked bivalve molluscs are packed for transport and distribution only in containers that are sealed in a manner that readily allows detection of any tampering.

Information on sport caught fish containers | Section 54

54   (1) A seafood processor must ensure that marks made in accordance with this section are legible, readily visible and permanent.

  1. A seafood processor must ensure that each container of sport caught fish is marked with all of the following:

Fisheries | 5.4 Fishing, Harvesting & Controlling Aquatic Species | Instruction | 2 - Fish

  1. the species of fish in the container;

Species Status and Assessment | 4 - Governance

  1. the name of the seafood processor, as shown on the seafood processor’s licence, and the address of the seafood processor;

  2. the date on which the fish were processed;

  3. the words, “sport caught fish — not for sale”.

Fisheries | 5.4 Fishing, Harvesting & Controlling Aquatic Species | 2 - Fish

  1. A seafood processor must ensure that each carton of containers of sport caught fish is marked with all of the following:

Fisheries | 5.4 Fishing, Harvesting & Controlling Aquatic Species | Instruction | 2 - Fish

  1. the information required under subsection (2) (b) and (d);

  2. the name of the fisher who harvested the fish.

Fisheries | 5.4 Fishing, Harvesting & Controlling Aquatic Species | 2 - Fish

  1. For the purposes of subsection (2) (c), the date must be expressed in the format “year month day”, as follows:

  1. the year must be expressed by using all 4 numerals that comprise the year;

  2. the month must be expressed by using the code that corresponds to the month as shown in the table below:

  3. the day must be expressed by using the 2 numerals that comprise the calendar date, with the first numeral being “0” if the calendar date is less than 10.

Tracking system for sport caught fish | Section 55

55   (1) A seafood processor who processes sport caught fish must ensure that processed sport caught fish are distributed only to the fisher who harvested the fish.

Fisheries | 5.4 Fishing, Harvesting & Controlling Aquatic Species | Instruction | 2 - Fish

  1. For the purpose of subsection (1), a seafood processor must have in place a system that does all of the following:
  1. marks or otherwise identifies sport caught fish, on receipt for processing, in a manner that enables a person to readily determine the fisher of the sport caught fish;

Fisheries | 5.4 Fishing, Harvesting & Controlling Aquatic Species | 2 - Fish

  1. maintains the mark or other identification throughout processing and until distribution;

  2. verifies on distribution that the recipient of the processed sport caught fish is the fisher.

Fisheries | 5.4 Fishing, Harvesting & Controlling Aquatic Species | 2 - Fish

Seafood processor receipt and distribution records | Section 56

56   (1) A seafood processor must keep records, in accordance with this section, with respect to each delivery of fish and aquatic plants

  1. received by the seafood processor for processing, and

  2. distributed by the seafood processor.

  1. Records must include at least the following information:

  1. if applicable, the licence number or federal licence number of the person from whom fish or aquatic plants were received;

  2. the contact information of the person

  3. from whom fish or aquatic plants were received, or

  1. to whom fish or aquatic plants were distributed;

  2. the date of receipt or transport for distribution;

  3. the quantity of

  4. fish received or distributed, divided according to species and, once processed, manner of processing, and

  5. aquatic plants received or distributed, divided according to aquatic plant group and aquatic plant species;

  1. the amount paid or received for fish and aquatic plants received or distributed;

  2. the contact information of the transporter that distributed the fish or aquatic plants.

  1. A seafood processor that distributes bivalve molluscs must do both of the following:

  1. in addition to the information required under subsection (2), include the information contained on the tag referred to in section 53 (1) (b) [processing bivalve molluscs];

  2. provide to a transporter of the bivalve molluscs a copy of the information referred to in paragraph (a).

Other seafood processor records | Section 57

57   (1) In this section:

“custom processing” means the processing of fish and aquatic plants for the purpose of returning the fish and aquatic plants to the person from whom they were received;

“processing for distribution” means the processing of fish and aquatic plants for the purpose of distributing the fish and aquatic plants to persons other than the person from whom they were received.

  1. A seafood processor must keep records, in accordance with this section, with respect to each calendar month or part of a calendar month the seafood processor is engaged in activities under the licence.

  2. Employment records must include at least the following information:

  1. the number of employees, divided according to the type of activity in which those employees are primarily employed;

  2. the number of employees engaged in custom processing activities, with those activities divided according to species.

  1. Processing records must include at least the following information, divided according to custom processing activities and processing for distribution activities:

  1. the total quantity of fish and aquatic plants received by the seafood processor;

  2. the total quantity of fish and aquatic plants processed by the seafood processor, divided according to species and manner of processing.

Operational requirements | Section 58

58   (1) A transporter must ensure that all equipment the transporter uses to transport fish and aquatic plants is constructed from materials that

  1. are durable and suitable for their intended purpose, and

  2. ensure that food contact surfaces are easily cleaned and free from any noxious or toxic substance.

Pollution | 9.1 Water-Borne & Other Effluent Pollution | 3 - Habitat

  1. A transporter must ensure that all equipment the transporter uses to store fish and aquatic plants is constructed in a manner that protects the fish and aquatic plants from becoming unsafe food.

Temperature of transported fish | Section 59

59   (1) A transporter of fish must ensure that the temperature of fish being transported is maintained in accordance with section 40 (1) [temperature, water and ice standards].

  1. A transporter of fish must comply with section 40 (2) as if the transporter were a seafood processor.

Live bivalve mollusc transporter records | Section 60

60   (1) A transporter of live bivalve molluscs must carry during transport the record referred to in section 56 (3) (b) [seafood processor receipt and distribution records].

  1. A transporter must provide the record referred to in section 56 (3) (b) to the person who receives the bivalve molluscs.

Must keep record of live bivalve molluscs | Section 61

61   A person who receives live bivalve molluscs from a transporter must do both of the following:

  1. add to the record received under section 60 (2) [live bivalve mollusc transporter records] a notation of the date on which the bivalve molluscs were received;

  2. keep the record referred to in paragraph (a) for at least one year.

No distribution of unlawfully processed aquatic plants | Section 62

62   A person must not distribute, or offer to distribute, to the public for human consumption an aquatic plant that has been processed by a person other than a person who holds, or who is exempt from holding, a seafood processor licence.

How to express quantity | Section 63

63   Subject to section 14 [wild aquatic plant harvester records], a person who must keep a record of the quantity of fish or aquatic plants grown, harvested, received, distributed or transported, must express the quantity as follows:

  1. with respect to fish or aquatic plants grown, harvested or received, in kilograms or tonnes;

  2. with respect to fish or aquatic plants distributed or transported, in kilograms, tonnes or as the number of cartons distributed, if a description is given of the

  3. number of containers in each carton, and

  1. the weight of each container.

How to express amounts paid and received | Section 64

64   A person who must keep a record of the amount paid or received for fish and aquatic plants received or distributed, must express the amount in Canadian dollars.

Records to be kept for 3 years | Section 65

65   Subject to any provision to the contrary, a person who must keep records under this regulation must ensure that each record is kept for a period of at least 3 years.

Reporting information to minister | Section 66

66   (1) Subject to subsection (2) and the terms of an applicable harvest agreement, if any, a person who must keep a record under this regulation, other than a transporter, must report to the minister the information, or a consolidation of the information, that the person must keep

  1. annually, for the period beginning January 1 and ending December 31, and

  2. as required by the minister.

  1. Subsection (1) (a) does not apply to the following records:

  1. harvest records prepared under section 14 [wild aquatic plant harvester records];

  2. records respecting food safety plans prepared under section 39 [food safety plans];

  3. records respecting sanitation plans prepared under section 41 [sanitation plans].

Factors relating to objectives set by government for timber | Section 1.1

1.1   The following factors apply to a result or strategy for the objectives set out in section 6 [objectives set by government for timber]:

  1. the importance of retaining suitable secondary structure to maintain or enhance the future timber supply;

  2. retaining attributes of suitable secondary structure in terms of

  3. density, height or other attributes suitable for assessing expected growth and yield of timber, and

  1. the minimum size of areas of suitable secondary structure necessary to provide commercial harvesting opportunities in the future;

  2. considerations involved in determining where it is practicable to retain suitable secondary structure, including considerations of safety and conservation of forest resources.

Activities and categories of persons prescribed for forest practices | Section 1.2

1.2   (1) The following activities are prescribed for the purposes of the definition of “forest practice” in section 1 (1) of the Act:

  1. timber harvesting, road construction, road maintenance, road use, road deactivation, silviculture treatments, botanical forest product collecting and fire use, control and suppression;

  2. an activity carried out under an agreement under the Forest Act, a special use permit or a road use permit;

  3. an activity related to an activity described in paragraph (a) or (b).

  1. The following categories of persons are prescribed for the purposes of paragraph (c) of the definition of “forest practice” in section 1 (1) of the Act:

  1. contractors, employees and agents of a holder of an agreement under the Forest Act or the Range Act;

  2. persons with an obligation to establish a free growing stand in accordance with an agreement made under section 29.1 of the Act;

  3. a holder of a special use permit that authorizes the holder to manage or use Crown land for silviculture treatments or wildlife habitat enhancement.

Authorization to cut | Section 4

4   (1) The following enactments are prescribed enactments for the purposes of section 52 (1) (e) (ii) [unauthorized timber harvesting] of the Act:

  1. this regulation;

  2. the Mineral Tenure Act, for the purpose of locating a claim.

(1.1) An agreement holder and the timber sales manager may cut, damage or destroy Crown timber as necessary for the purpose of carrying out silviculture treatments, stand tending treatments or forest health treatments.

  1. A free miner under the Mineral Tenure Act may cut, damage or destroy Crown timber before the free miner requires a permit under section 10 [permits] of the Mines Act if Crown timber is cut, damaged or destroyed only

  1. by hand held tools, and

  2. for the purpose of mineral exploration.

(2.1) A land surveyor may cut, damage or destroy Crown timber as necessary in the course of carrying out duties as a land surveyor.

  1. Except for minor clearing of brush and downed trees, subsection (2) does not permit cutting, damaging or destroying Crown timber beyond the minimum necessary for the safety of persons carrying out the activities.

[am. B.C. Regs. 580/2004, s. 4; 320/2006, s. 1.]

Factors relating to objective set by government for cultural heritage resources | Section 4

4   The following factors apply to a result or strategy for the objective set out in section 10 [objectives set by government for cultural heritage resources]:

  1. the relative value or importance of a particular cultural heritage resource to a traditional use by an aboriginal people;

  2. the relative abundance or scarcity of a cultural heritage resource that is the focus of a traditional use by an aboriginal people;

  3. the historical extent of a traditional use by an aboriginal people of a cultural heritage resource;

  4. the impact on government granted timber harvesting rights of conserving or protecting a cultural heritage resource that is the focus of a traditional use by an aboriginal people;

  5. options for mitigating the impact that a forest practice might have on a cultural heritage resource that is the focus of a traditional use by an aboriginal people.

Removing Crown timber to protect a community from wildfire | Section 4.01

4.01   The minister may exempt a person from section 52 (3) of the Act if the minister is satisfied that the Crown timber to be removed

  1. is non-merchantable timber,

  2. is to be removed for the purpose of protecting a community from wildfire, and

  3. will not be sold to others.

[en. B.C. Reg. 224/2006, s. 1.]

Definitions for Part 1.1 | Section 4.02

4.02   In this Part:

“additional measure” means a measure included in a forest operations plan that imposes a requirement on the holder of the forest operations plan other than or in addition to one or more of the following requirements:

  1. a planning guideline requirement;

  2. a substituted requirement;

  3. a practice requirement set out in Part 4 of this regulation;

“amendment” means an amendment to a forest operations plan;

“existing cutblock”, in relation to a holder of a forest operations plan, means a cutblock

  1. for which the holder has been granted a cutting permit or for which the holder has issued a timber sales licence, or

  2. in which the holder has harvested timber under an agreement;

“existing road”, in relation to a holder of a forest operations plan, means a road that the holder is authorized to construct or has constructed under a cutting permit or road permit;

“forest operations plan requirement” includes the following requirements in relation to a forest operations plan:

  1. a planning guideline requirement;

  2. a substituted requirement;

  3. a practice requirement set out in Part 4 of this regulation from which the holder of the forest operations plan is not exempt;

  4. an additional measure;

“planning guideline requirement” means a requirement included under section 2.28 (2) (c) [planning guidelines regarding forest practices, silvicultural systems or stocking standards] of the Act in a planning guideline;

“substituted requirement” means a requirement substituted under section 2.37 (2) (b) [additional requirements if forest operations plan is inconsistent with planning guidelines] of the Act for a planning guideline requirement.

[en. B.C. Reg. 219/2024, Sch. 1, s. 2.]

Information requirements for forest operations plan | Section 4.03

4.03   A person who submits or holds a forest operations plan must include in the plan all of the information required under this Division.

[en. B.C. Reg. 219/2024, Sch. 1, s. 2.]

Business contact information | Section 4.04

4.04   (1) A forest operations plan must include the following current information in relation to the person who is or will be the holder of the plan:

  1. the person’s name;

  2. the person’s address in British Columbia, other than a post office box;

  3. regular business hours;

  4. email address;

  5. website address, if applicable.

  1. A forest operations plan held by more than one person must include the information referred to in subsection (1) in relation to each holder.

  2. A forest operations plan must be amended if information included under this section changes or is no longer accurate.

[en. B.C. Reg. 219/2024, Sch. 1, s. 2.]

Identification number and amendment number | Section 4.05

4.05   A forest operations plan must

  1. include a unique name, number or code for the purposes of identifying the plan, and

  2. if the plan has been amended, indicate the number of times the plan has been amended.

[en. B.C. Reg. 219/2024, Sch. 1, s. 2.]

Date of approval | Section 4.06

4.06   (1) A forest operations plan or amendment must include the date on which the plan or amendment is submitted to the minister for approval.

  1. After a forest operations plan or amendment has been approved, the plan must be amended to include the date on which the plan or amendment was approved.

[en. B.C. Reg. 219/2024, Sch. 1, s. 2.]

Term and expiry | Section 4.07

4.07   After a forest operations plan or amendment has been approved, the plan must be amended to include

  1. the term of the plan, and

  2. the date on which the plan will expire.

[en. B.C. Reg. 219/2024, Sch. 1, s. 2.]

Date of extension | Section 4.08

4.08   After a forest operations plan has been extended under section 2.43 [extension of term of forest operations plan] of the Act, the plan must be amended to include

  1. the date on which the minister extended the term of the plan, and

  2. the date on which the extended plan will expire.

[en. B.C. Reg. 219/2024, Sch. 1, s. 2.]

Forest region and forest district | Section 4.09

4.09   A forest operations plan must identify the forest districts and forest regions, as those terms are defined under the Forest Act, in which the forest operations area is located.

[en. B.C. Reg. 219/2024, Sch. 1, s. 2.]

Cutblocks and roads | Section 4.11

4.11   (1) A forest operations plan must list

  1. each existing cutblock and proposed cutblock, and

  2. each existing road and proposed road.

  1. A forest operations plan must identify each proposed cutblock and proposed road with a unique name, number or code.

  2. A forest operations plan held by more than one person must list the cutblocks and roads referred to in subsection (1) according to which person proposes the harvesting of timber on the cutblock or the construction of the road.

[en. B.C. Reg. 219/2024, Sch. 1, s. 2.]

Commencement dates | Section 4.12

4.12   A forest operations plan must include, for each cutblock and road proposed in the plan, the year in which the person who will hold the forest operations plan proposes to begin

  1. harvesting timber on the cutblock, or

  2. constructing the road.

[en. B.C. Reg. 219/2024, Sch. 1, s. 2.]

Assessments | Section 4.13

4.13   If a planning guideline requires an assessment to be conducted before a forest operations plan or an amendment is submitted to the minister for approval, a copy of the assessment must be submitted to the minister together with the plan or amendment.

Specifying stocking standards in forest operations plan | Section 4.14

4.14   (1) A forest operations plan must specify the situations or circumstances that determine when section 44 (1) [free growing stands generally] or section 45 [free growing stands collectively across cutblocks] will apply to an area.

  1. The forest operations plan must specify the following for each of the situations or circumstances specified under subsection (1) of this section:

  1. if section 44 (1) (a) will apply, the regeneration date and stocking standards;

  2. if section 44 (1) (b) will apply, the free growing height and stocking standards;

  3. if section 45 (1) will apply, the regeneration date and the stocking standards;

  4. if section 45 (2) will apply, the free growing date and the stocking standards, as approved by the chief forester.

  1. The forest operations plan must specify stocking standards for areas referred to in section 44 (4) and the situations or circumstances that determine when the stocking standards will be applied.

  2. This section does not apply if the forest operations plan incorporates by reference a planning guideline requirement that specifies stocking standards for the forest operations area.

Public review and comment period | Section 4.33

4.33   (1) The person must make the forest operations plan publicly available for review and comment for a period of 60 days, unless the minister authorizes a shorter period under subsection (2).

  1. The minister may authorize a shorter public review and comment period of not less than 10 days if the minister is satisfied that the 60-day period under subsection (1) would likely result in

  1. an unacceptable impact on the proper management and conservation of forests and forest ecosystems,

  2. an increased risk of wildfire, or

  3. an increased risk to public safety.

  1. The person must publish notice of the review and comment period described in subsection (1) of this section on a publicly accessible website maintained by or on behalf of the person and in one of the following:

  1. a newspaper published in British Columbia and circulating in the areas subject to the forest operations plan;

  2. the Gazette.

Criteria for minister’s approval of forest operations plan | Section 4.39

4.39   The minister must not approve a forest operations plan or amendment unless the minister is satisfied that the following criteria are met:

  1. the forest operations plan includes planning guideline requirements, substituted requirements or additional measures respecting the matters referred to in section 2.28 (2) (a) to (c) of the Act that are measurable or verifiable;

  2. the forest operations plan sufficiently supports

  3. the objectives set out in section 2.22 [preparation of forest landscape plan] of the Act, and

Forest and Range | 5.3 Logging, Harvesting & Controlling Trees | Interpretation & Purpose | 3 - Habitat

  1. any objectives established under section 2.51 [decision-making agreement — statutory power of decision of chief forester] of the Act by a decision-making agreement;

  2. the forest operations plan is not likely to result in an increased fire hazard within a wildland urban interface area;

  3. the forest operations plan is not likely to result in an increased risk to public safety;

  1. the forest operations plan is not likely to negatively impact cultural heritage resources;

  2. the cumulative impact of the forest operations plans in an area is not likely to

  3. exceed a threshold established in a forest operations plan requirement, or

  1. prevent the achievement of one or more outcomes of the applicable forest landscape plan.

Forest and Range | 5.3 Logging, Harvesting & Controlling Trees | 3 - Habitat

[en. B.C. Reg. 219/2024, Sch. 1, s. 2.]

When site level plan not required for cutblocks | Section 4.59

4.59   The holder of a forest operations plan is not required to prepare a site level plan under section 2.47 (1) (a) [site level plans for cutblocks] of the Act if one or more of the following circumstances applies:

  1. timber harvesting must proceed expeditiously to eliminate a safety hazard;

  2. timber harvesting is needed to facilitate collection of seed, leaving an opening not greater than 1 ha;

  3. timber harvesting is limited to a volume of 50 m3 or less;

  4. timber harvesting is restricted to one or more of the following:

  5. removing felled trees from landings and road rights of way;

  1. harvesting trees on land that is, or will be, exclusively used for harvesting hay or grazing livestock in accordance with an agreement under the Range Act;

  2. harvesting timber for experimental purposes if, in the opinion of the minister, the harvesting will be carried out under controlled scientific or investigative conditions;

  3. clearing areas for or within a recreation site or recreation trail;

  4. felling and removing trees that have been or will be treated to facilitate the entrapment of pests;

  5. commercial thinning, removal of individual trees, or a similar type of intermediate cutting;

  6. harvesting special forest products other than woodchips or hogged tree material.

[en. B.C. Reg. 219/2024, Sch. 1, s. 2.]

When site level plan not required for roads | Section 4.6

4.6   The holder of a forest operations plan is not required to prepare a site level plan under section 2.47 (1) (b) [site level plans for roads] of the Act if the timber harvesting is limited to removal of timber to improve safety for road users by

  1. eliminating a safety hazard,

  2. improving visibility, or

  3. increasing the number of pullouts or the size of existing pullouts.

[en. B.C. Reg. 219/2024, Sch. 1, s. 2.]

Objectives set by government for timber | Section 6

6   The objectives set by government for timber are to

  1. maintain or enhance an economically valuable supply of commercial timber from British Columbia’s forests,

  2. ensure that delivered wood costs, generally, after taking into account the effect on them of the relevant provisions of this regulation and of the Act, are competitive in relation to equivalent costs in relation to regulated primary forest activities in other jurisdictions, and

  3. ensure that the provisions of this regulation and of the Act that pertain to primary forest activities do not unduly constrain the ability of a holder of an agreement under the Forest Act to exercise the holder’s rights under the agreement.

Factors relating to stocking specifications | Section 6

6   (1) In this section:

“even-aged stand” means a stand of trees consisting of only one or two age classes;

  1. The following factors apply to the development of stocking standards, generally:

  1. the long term forest health risks that are relevant to species selection for the purposes of establishing a free growing stand under section 29 [free growing stands] of the Act;

  2. the occurrence and extent of forest health factors.

  1. The following factors apply to the development of stocking standards under section 16 (2) [stocking standards]:

  1. for an area that is managed as an even-aged stand,

  2. the characteristics, quantity and distribution of retained trees referred to in subparagraph (ii).

  1. The following factors apply to developing stocking standards under section 16 (4):

  1. the types of commercially valuable and ecologically suitable species that should be retained on the area;

Identifying forest development units | Section 14

14   (1) A person required to prepare a forest stewardship plan may specify in the plan or an amendment to it,

  1. a new forest development unit,

  2. a forest development unit that is in effect on the date of the submission of the forest stewardship plan to the minister,

  3. an area to which section 196 (1) or (2) of the Act is applicable that is in a forest development unit referred to in paragraph (a) or (b) of this subsection,

  4. an area to which section 197 (4) or (7) of the Act is applicable that is in a forest development unit referred to in paragraph (a) or (b) of this subsection, or

  5. cutblocks to which section 197 (5) of the Act is applicable that is in a forest development unit referred to in paragraph (a) or (b) of this subsection.

  1. A person required to prepare a forest stewardship plan must ensure that the plan identifies for the forest development units specified under subsection (1) those things described in subsection (3) that

  1. are in the forest development unit, and

  2. are in effect

  3. on the date the plan or amendment to it is submitted for approval, if the plan is submitted on or before December 31, 2005, or

  1. 4 months before the date the plan or amendment to it, as the case may be, is submitted for approval, if the plan or amendment to it is submitted after December 31, 2005.
  1. The things that under subsection (2) are to be identified in a forest stewardship plan referred to in that subsection are each

  1. ungulate winter range,

  2. wildlife habitat area,

Species Status and Assessment | Designation | 4 - Governance

  1. fisheries sensitive watershed,

Fisheries | 5.4 Fishing, Harvesting & Controlling Aquatic Species | 2 - Fish

Water Use and Watercourse Modifications | 7.2 Dams & Water Management / Use | 3 - Habitat

  1. lakeshore management zone, including specifying the width of the zone, if the zone is identified on a map accompanying the establishment of the lakeshore management zone,

  2. scenic area,

  3. lake identified as an L1 lake under section 49 (1) (b) (ii) if the lake has been identified on a map accompanying the identification,

  4. community watershed,

Water Use and Watercourse Modifications | 7.2 Dams & Water Management / Use | 3 - Habitat

  1. old growth management area,

  2. area in which commercial timber harvesting is prohibited by another enactment,

  3. cutting permit and road permit held by the agreement holder if that is the person required to prepare the plan, and

  4. road permit or timber sale licence issued or entered into by the timber sales manager if the timber sales manager is the person required to prepare the plan.

  1. A person who prepares a forest stewardship plan may identify an area as a declared area if, on the date that the area is identified,

  1. the area is in a forest development unit in effect, and

  2. all activities and evaluations that are necessary in relation to inclusion of cutblocks and roads in the area have been completed.

[en. B.C. Reg. 580/2004, s. 13; am. B.C. Regs. 62/2005, s. 6; 64/2021, s. 2; 62/2024, Sch., s. 34.]

Stocking standards | Section 16

16   (1) A person required to prepare a forest stewardship plan must ensure that the plan specifies the situations or circumstances that determine when section 44 (1) [free growing stands generally] or section 45 [free growing stands collectively across cutblocks] will apply to an area.

  1. In specifying a stocking standard under this section, a person who prepares a forest stewardship plan may consider the factors set out in section 6 [factors relating to stocking standards] of Schedule 1.

  2. A person required to prepare a forest stewardship plan must ensure that the plan specifies, for each of the situations or circumstances specified under subsection (1) where

  1. section 44 (1) (a) will apply, the regeneration date and stocking standards,

  2. section 44 (1) (b) will apply, the free growing height and stocking standards,

  3. section 45 (1) will apply, the regeneration date and the stocking standards, and

  4. section 45 (2) will apply, the free growing date and the stocking standards, as approved by the chief forester.

  1. A person required to prepare a forest stewardship plan must ensure that the plan specifies stocking standards for areas referred to in section 44 (4), and the situations or circumstances that determine when the stocking standards will be applied.

[am. B.C. Regs. 62/2005, s. 3; 102/2005, s. 1; 62/2024, Sch., s. 35.]

Order specifying new stocking standard | Section 16.1

16.1   (1) The chief forester may make an order under section 31.1 of the Act requiring the holder of a forest stewardship plan to comply with stocking standards set out in the order if the chief forester

  1. has information relating to forest health, natural hazards or ecological conditions in the area covered by the forest stewardship plan that was not available when the plan was approved,

Spatial Designation | Designation | 4 - Governance

  1. is satisfied that either of the following applies:

  2. the stocking standard specified under section 16 of this regulation does not adequately address any of the following matters in relation to the area covered by the forest stewardship plan:

  1. ecological sustainability or ecological resilience;

Spatial Designation | 4 - Governance

  1. wildfire risk reduction;

  2. the preservation of non-timber stewardship values, including the forest ecosystems or non-timber forest resources of interest to First Nation groups;

  1. the stocking standard specified under section 16 of this regulation is not consistent with the timber supply analysis and forest management assumptions that apply to the area covered by the forest stewardship plan, and

  2. is satisfied that the continuation of the stocking standard specified under section 16 of this regulation would

  3. have unacceptable adverse effects on any of the following:

  1. forest resources or range resources;

  2. the matters set out in paragraph (b) (i) (A) or (C), or

  1. increase wildfire risk to an unacceptable level.

  1. The chief forester may make an order referred to in subsection (1) at any time during the term of the forest stewardship plan.

  2. An order referred to in subsection (1) applies to any cutblock, in the area covered by the forest stewardship plan, in which harvesting has not yet begun.

  3. Before making an order referred to in subsection (1), the chief forester must consider both of the following:

  1. the financial impact of the order on the holder of the forest stewardship plan;

  2. whether complying with the order is practicable, given the circumstances or conditions applicable to the area covered by the forest stewardship plan.

[en. B.C. Reg. 57/2024, Sch. 2, s. 1.]

Invasive plants | Section 17

17   For the purpose of section 47 [invasive plants] of the Act, a person who prepares a forest stewardship plan must specify measures in the plan to prevent the introduction or spread of species of plants that are invasive plants under the Invasive Plants Regulation, if the introduction or spread is likely to be the result of the person’s forest practices.

Invasive Species and Disease | 8.1 Invasive Non-Native / Alien Species | Interpretation & Purpose | 3 - Habitat

[am. B.C. Reg. 580/2004, s. 15.]

Natural range barriers | Section 18

18   For the purpose of section 48 [natural range barriers] of the Act, a person who prepares a forest stewardship plan must specify measures to mitigate the effect of removing or rendering ineffective natural range barriers.

Cumulative effect of multiple forest stewardship plans | Section 19

19   For the purpose of section 9 [proportional objectives] of the Act, the minister may establish targets referred to in that section, if, where there are likely to be multiple forest stewardship plans within an area,

  1. one or more holders of a forest stewardship plan may be unduly constrained in the specifying of results or strategies in the holder’s plan unless targets are established under section 9 of the Act, and

  2. the holders of a forest stewardship plan within the area are unable to reach an agreement that would remove the constraints referred to in paragraph (a).

[am. B.C. Regs. 321/2006, s. 10; 163/2023, Sch. 2, s. 2.]

Limited content forest stewardship plans | Section 19.1

19.1   The minister may exempt the holder of

  1. a forestry licence to cut that is a major licence, or

from one or more of the requirements of Divisions 1 and 2 if the minister is satisfied that the exemption is appropriate, given the nature and extent of the timber harvesting proposed by the holder.

[en. B.C. Reg. 580/2004, s. 17; am. B.C. Regs. 106/2009, s. 1 (a); 158/2023, Sch. 2, s. 1.]

When forest stewardship plan not required | Section 19.2

19.2   For the purpose of section 4 (2) of the Act, the holder of a forestry licence to cut entered into under section 47.3 (1) (a) of the Forest Act is not required to prepare a forest stewardship plan under section 3 (1) of the Act if timber harvesting under the licence is restricted to an area which is subject to a contract that

  1. provides for the preparation of the area for reforestation,

  2. is funded under a vote as defined in section 1 of the Financial Administration Act, and

  3. is under a program administered by the minister.

[en. B.C. Reg. 106/2009, s. 1 (b); am. B.C. Reg. 219/2024, Sch. 1, s. 4.]

Providing notice | Section 20

20   (1) Before a person submits to the minister for approval a forest stewardship plan or an amendment to one, the person must publish a notice at least once in a newspaper, and may publish the notice more frequently, stating

  1. that the plan or amendment is publicly available for review and for written comment at the person’s place of business or at another place specified in the notice,

  2. persons may attend at that place during business hours to review the plan or amendment, and

  3. the address of the person proposing the plan or amendment to which address persons may submit written comments about the plan by mail or in person.

  1. For the purposes of subsection (1), the period during which persons have the opportunity to review a forest stewardship plan or an amendment to one begins on the date the notice is first published and ends

  1. 60 days after that date, if no greater or lesser number of days is determined under paragraph (b) or (c) and paragraph (d) is inapplicable,

  2. a greater number of days after that date that the minister may determine if paragraph (d) is inapplicable and the minister considers that the greater number of days is necessary to provide an adequate opportunity for review and comment under section 21,

  3. a lesser number of days that the minister may determine if paragraph (d) is inapplicable and the minister considers that the lesser number of days will provide an adequate opportunity for review and comment under section 21, or

  4. 10 days after that date if all or a substantial part of the timber to which the plan pertains

  5. is dead, infested with pests or otherwise damaged, or is required to be harvested to facilitate the removal of dead, infested or damaged timber, and

  1. must be harvested expeditiously to prevent

  1. the spread of pests, or

  2. a significant reduction in the economic value of the timber due to a deterioration in the quality of the timber.

  1. The minister by order may grant an exemption to a person who proposes a forest stewardship plan or an amendment to one from the requirement to publish a notice under subsection (1).

  2. If the minister makes an order under subsection (3) and the forest stewardship plan or amendment is approved, the person exempted under the order must publish in a newspaper a notice specifying

  1. that the forest stewardship plan or the amendment has been approved without having been made publicly available for review and comment, and

  2. the date on which operations under the plan have been authorized to begin.

  1. Despite subsection (1), a person who proposes an amendment to a forest stewardship plan in respect of section 16 is not required to publish a notice in a newspaper.

  2. Despite subsection (1), a person who prepares and submits to the minister an amendment to a forest stewardship plan under section 12.21 (1) or (2) is not required to publish a notice in a newspaper.

[en. B.C. Reg. 580/2004, s. 18; am. B.C. Regs. 182/2008, s. 3; 64/2021, s. 2.]

Review and comment | Section 21

21   (1) A person who publishes a notice under section 20 (1), during the applicable period referred to in section 20 (2),

  1. if required by the minister, must refer a copy of the forest stewardship plan, or a portion of the plan, to

  2. any agency of government, or

  1. any agency of the Government of Canada,

  1. must provide a person who is interested in the plan with an opportunity to review the plan during normal business hours at the place of business of the person who published the notice or other venue specified in the notice under section 20 (1),

  2. must provide a person whose rights may be affected by the plan with an opportunity to review the plan in a manner that is commensurate with the nature and extent to which the person’s rights may be affected,

(c.1) must refer a copy of the plan to a timber sales manager who may be affected by the plan, and

  1. must make reasonable efforts to meet with First Nation groups affected by the plan to discuss the plan.
  1. A person given the opportunity to review or discuss the plan under subsection (1) may submit written comments in respect of the plan during the period and to the address specified in the notice under section 20 (1).

[en. B.C. Reg. 580/2004, s. 18; am. B.C. Reg. 321/2006, s. 11.]

Responding to review and comment | Section 22

  1. must consider any written comments received under section 21 that are

  2. areas described in section 14 (1) (b), (c) or (d), (3) (j) or (k) or (4), or

  1. results and strategies that relate to the areas referred to in subparagraph (i).
  1. A person who submits a forest stewardship plan to the minister for approval must submit with the proposed plan

  1. a copy of the notice published under section 20,

  2. a copy of each written comment received under section 21,

  3. a description of any changes made to the plan as a result of the comments received under section 21, and

Consistency of results and strategies with established objectives | Section 25

25   (1) An intended result or strategy is not inconsistent with an established objective only because it

  1. is capable of producing a condition outside the range of natural variation characteristic of a season, an area or a forest resource,

  2. proposes an innovative means of addressing the established objective, or

  3. is based on a factor other than one specified in Schedule 1.

  1. On application by a person required to prepare a forest stewardship plan, the minister responsible for the Land Act may exempt the person from the requirement that an intended result or strategy specified in the plan, in relation to an objective that was

  1. established or continued under section 3 or 4 of the Forest Practices Code of British Columbia Act, and

  2. in effect on January 31, 2004,

be consistent with the objective, if the minister determines that requiring the result or strategy to be consistent with the objective would

  1. have a material adverse impact on the delivered wood costs of a holder of an agreement under the Forest Act to which the plan applies, and

  2. unduly constrain the ability of a holder referred to in paragraph (c) to exercise the holder’s rights under the agreement, and

the material adverse impact and undue constraint outweigh the benefits to the public that would be achieved by requiring the result or strategy to be consistent with the objective.

  1. In making a determination under section 16 of the Act in respect of a forest stewardship plan or an amendment to a forest stewardship plan, the minister responsible for the Forest Act must consider any exemption granted by the minister responsible for the Land Act under subsection (2) of this section.

Consistency of intended results and strategies with objectives | Section 25.1

25.1   (1) For the purpose of section 5 (1.1) of the Act, each intended result or strategy in a forest stewardship plan must be consistent with the established objectives to the extent practicable, to take into account the circumstances or conditions applicable to that area or that part.

  1. If an established objective is comprised of measurable or verifiable steps, processes or outcomes, an intended result or strategy that

  1. is specified in a forest stewardship plan for that objective,

  2. restates the same measurable or verifiable steps, practices or outcomes, and

  3. describes the circumstances in which those measurable or verifiable steps, practices or outcomes are to be achieved or carried out,

is to be considered to be consistent with objectives set by government and with the other established objectives to the extent practicable, as described in subsection (1) of this section.

34.8   For the purposes of section 15.2 (2) (a) (iii) of the Act, a forest operations map prepared by a timber sales manager must

  1. be of a scale and size that the minister considers sufficient for meaningful review and comment, and

  2. identify

  3. the timber sales manager who prepared the map,

  1. the BC timber sales business area to which the timber sales manager is appointed, and

  2. the forest stewardship plan to which the map relates.

[en. B.C. Reg. 163/2023, Sch. 6, s. 2.]

Publication of notice — timber sales manager | Section 34.9

34.9   (1) For the purposes of making a forest operations map publicly available for review and comment under section 15.2 (2) (b) of the Act, a timber sales manager must, at least 30 days before the date the operating period to which the map relates begins, publish a notice that meets the requirements set out in subsection (2)

  1. on a publicly accessible website maintained by or on behalf of the timber sales manager or the government, and

  2. at least once in a newspaper.

  1. A notice referred to in subsection (1) must include the following information, which must be the same in each notice:

  1. a statement that the map is publicly available for review and comment at the office of the timber sales manager or at another place specified in the notice;

  2. the beginning and end dates of the period during which persons may review the map and provide comments;

  3. an address at which and the hours during which persons may attend at the place to review the map;

  4. if applicable, a website address at which the map may be accessed;

  5. details regarding how comments may be submitted, including

  6. an address for personal delivery and the hours during which comments may be delivered,

  1. a mailing address,

  2. an email address, and

  3. if applicable, a website address for online submission;

  1. a statement that the timber sales manager may

  2. invite applications for timber sales licences for the harvesting of cutblocks shown on the map, and

  1. apply for road permits to construct roads shown on the map.
  1. For the purposes of subsection (2) (b), the period during which persons may review and provide comments in relation to the map

  1. subject to subsection (4), begins on the date specified in the notices published under subsection (1), and

  2. ends

  3. 30 days after that date, if no lesser number of days is determined under subparagraph (ii), or

  1. a lesser number of days after that date that the minister may determine if the minister considers that the lesser number of days is necessary in order to respond to risks relating to the environment, forest health or wildfire.

Spatial Designation | Authorization & Mandate | 4 - Governance

  1. The review period for a forest operations map must not begin until the notice required under subsection (1) in relation to the map has been published both on a publicly accessible website and at least once in a newspaper.

  1. An agreement holder other than a holder of a minor tenure or a fibre supply licence to cut, which holder is carrying out timber harvesting, must not cause the amount of soil disturbance on the net area to be reforested to exceed the following limits:

Use of seed | Section 43

43   (1) In this section, “transfer” means the process by which seed is selected and used, based on the origin of the seed and its genetic suitability for the site on which trees grown from the seed are to be planted.

  1. The chief forester may make standards for matters referred to in section 169 (1) (a) (i) to (v) [chief forester standards for forest practices] of the Act if the chief forester considers such standards to be necessary or appropriate for the purpose of regulating the use, registration, storage, selection or transfer of seed to be used in the establishment of free growing stands.

  2. The chief forester may authorize a person to exercise a discretion of the chief forester described in subsection (5), (6) or (7).

  3. Unless an alternative is approved under subsection (6), a person who plants trees while establishing a free growing stand must use only seed registered, stored, selected and transferred in accordance with the standards, if any, established by the chief forester.

  4. A person referred to in subsection (4) may submit to the chief forester for approval an alternative to any standard established by the chief forester under subsection (2).

  5. The chief forester may approve an alternative submitted under subsection (5) if the chief forester considers that the alternative is consistent with achieving the intent of the standard.

  6. If the chief forester approves an alternative submitted under subsection (5), the person who submitted the alternative

  1. is exempt from the requirement of subsection (4) for which the alternative has been approved, and

  2. must comply with the alternative.

  1. A person who is required to establish a free growing stand must keep a record of the registration numbers of the seed that is used, if any, and a map of the location where the trees grown from the seed are planted.

Secondary structure retention in mountain pine beetle affected stands | Section 43.1

43.1   (1) A holder of a cutting permit, a forestry licence to cut that does not provide for cutting permits or a timber sale licence must not carry out timber harvesting in a targeted pine leading stand, unless

  1. it is necessary to fell or modify a tree that is a safety hazard and there is no other practicable option for addressing the safety hazard,

  2. the harvesting is necessary to construct a road in the targeted pine leading stand and there is no other practicable option for locating the road, or

  3. at the conclusion of timber harvesting, the holder retains an adequate stocking density of suitable secondary structure.

  1. Despite subsection (1), a holder of a cutting permit, a forestry licence to cut that does not provide for cutting permits or a timber sale licence may harvest timber in a targeted pine leading stand without retaining an adequate stocking density of suitable secondary structure if

  1. the timber in the stand is subject to a significant risk of blowdown,

  2. at the time of harvesting, at least 30% of the pine trees in the stand contain live mountain pine beetles,

  3. harvesting the timber is necessary to protect a community, or other area agreed to by the minister prior to harvesting, from wildfire, or

  4. harvesting the timber is necessary to facilitate collection of tree seed and the resulting opening does not exceed 1 ha.

  1. Without limiting the stocking standards applicable under section 29 (1) or (2) of the Act or section 46 of this regulation, if a person referred to in subsection (1) (c) carries out harvesting in a targeted pine leading stand that creates an obligation to establish a free growing stand, each tree of suitable secondary structure retained in the stand is considered to be a tree of a preferred species for the purpose of establishing a free growing stand on the area where the adequate stocking density of suitable secondary structure was retained.

  2. This section does not apply to

  1. an occupant licence to cut or a master licence to cut that provides for cutting permits,

  2. a forestry licence to cut entered into by a timber sales manager,

  3. a road permit,

  4. a community forest agreement,

  5. an area that is subject to

  6. a cutting permit that has been issued,

  1. a timber sale licence that has been advertised or entered into, or

  2. a forestry licence to cut that does not provide for cutting permits which has been entered into by the regional manager or district manager,

before this section comes into force,

  1. an area that is subject to a cutting permit, a forestry licence to cut that does not provide for cutting permits or a timber sale licence if the timber cruising or field layout for the cutting permit, forestry licence to cut or timber sale licence has been completed before this section comes into force,

  2. a cutblock, if the cutblock has been specified in a forest stewardship plan as an area to which section 196 (1) (a) of the Act applies, or

  3. an area depicted on a government-endorsed forest cover map which indicates that lodgepole pine is the leading tree species if a timber cruise of the timber on the area, or other process agreed to by the minister prior to harvesting, shows that lodgepole pine is not the leading tree species.

[en. B.C. Reg. 182/2008, s. 4.]

if satisfied that the designation is appropriate having regard to the allowable annual cut determination for the area.

before the order takes effect under subsection (2) (b), or

Free growing stands generally | Section 44

44   (1) A person who has an obligation to establish a free growing stand must establish, for areas that have been identified under section 16 (1) [stocking standards] or section 4.14 [specifying stocking standards in forest operations plan] as areas to which this section will apply, a stand that

  1. meets the applicable stocking standards set out in the forest stewardship plan for the area, by the applicable regeneration date specified for the area, and

  2. meets the applicable stocking standards and free growing height set out in the forest stewardship plan for the area by a free growing date that is no more than 20 years from the commencement date, unless the minister permits a later free growing date.

  1. If an agreement holder contravenes section 52 (1) [unauthorized timber harvesting] of the Act, the holder must establish, on the area on which the contravention occurred, a stand that meets the requirements specified in the holder’s forest stewardship plan or forest operations plan for an area with similar attributes, as if the area on which the contravention occurred had been identified under section 16 (1) or 4.14 as being subject to this section.

  2. A person is exempt from the requirements of section 29 (1) and (2) [free growing stands] of the Act in respect of an area if timber harvesting is restricted to one or more of the following:

  1. harvesting timber to eliminate a safety hazard;

  2. harvesting timber to facilitate the collection of seed, leaving an opening not greater than 1 ha;

  3. removing felled trees from landings and road rights of way;

  4. harvesting trees on land that is, or will be, exclusively used for harvesting hay or grazing livestock in accordance with an agreement under the Range Act;

  5. harvesting timber for experimental purposes if, in the opinion of the minister, the harvesting will be carried out under controlled scientific or investigative conditions;

  6. clearing areas for or within a recreation site or recreation trail;

  7. felling and removing trees that have been or will be treated to facilitate the entrapment of pests;

  8. commercial thinning, removal of individual trees, or a similar type of intermediate cutting;

  9. harvesting special forest products other than woodchips or hogged tree material.

  1. A person who harvests timber for the reasons referred to in subsection (3) (h) and (i) must ensure that, for a period of 12 months after completion of harvest, the area on which timber harvesting was carried out conforms to the stocking standards specified in section 16 (4) for the area.

[am. B.C. Regs. 580/2004, s. 33; 152/2007, s. 1; 157/2012, Sch. 4, s. 3; 219/2024, Sch. 1, ss. 9 and 10.]

Free growing stands collectively across cutblocks | Section 45

45   (1) If a person specifies in a forest stewardship plan under section 16 (1) [specifying stocking standards in forest stewardship plan] or forest operations plan under section 4.14 [specifying stocking standards in forest operations plan] that the requirement to be met by the regeneration date relates to a group of cutblocks, the person must establish stands on the net areas to be reforested that conform to the applicable stocking standards by the applicable regeneration date, as identified under section 16 (3) (c).

  1. If a person specifies in a forest stewardship plan under section 16 (1) or forest operations plan under section 4.14 that the requirement to be met by the free growing date relates to a group of cutblocks, the person must establish stands on the net areas to be reforested that conform to the applicable stocking standards by the applicable free growing date as identified under section 16 (3) (d).

Free growing stand — forestry licence to cut | Section 46

46   (1) Subject to subsections (3) and (3.1), if

  1. a cutblock is harvested under a forestry licence to cut that is not a major licence or a minor tenure, and

  2. 500 m3 or more of timber is harvested from the cutblock,

the minister, or the holder of a forestry licence to cut entered into by the minister responsible for the Resort Timber Administration Act, must establish a free growing stand in the net area to be reforested that

  1. conforms to the applicable stocking standards by the applicable regeneration date, and

Unless otherwise specified by the minister, the applicable stocking standards and applicable regeneration and free growing dates referred to in subsection (1) are those specified for that silviculture system and that biogeoclimatic ecosystem classification in the Ministry of Forests and Range’s publication, Reference Guide for Forest Development Plan Stocking Standards, as amended from time to time.

  2. The minister, or the holder of a forestry licence to cut entered into by the minister responsible for the Resort Timber Administration Act, is not required to establish a free growing stand under subsection (1) if the silvicultural system used on the area

  1. is clearcutting and the harvested area, if taken together with adjoining clearcut areas that are not occupied by free growing stands, does not exceed 1 ha, or

  2. is other than clearcutting and, at the completion of harvest, the trees retained on the harvested area conform to the specifications

  3. of the minister, if any, or

  1. for the applicable silvicultural system and biogeoclimatic ecosystem classification in the Ministry of Forests and Range’s publication, Reference Guide for Forest Development Plan Stocking Standards, as amended from time to time.

(3.1) The minister is not required to establish a free growing stand under subsection (1) in respect of an area for which a forestry licence to cut has been issued in the circumstances described in section 4 [harvesting in conjunction with a government funded contract] of the Forestry Licence to Cut Regulation.

  1. The minister must consider the matters set out in section 26 (3) when making a decision respecting the applicable stocking standards and applicable regeneration and free growing dates under subsection (2).

  2. The minister must consider the matters set out in section 26 (4) when making a decision respecting the specifications described in subsection (3) (b) (i).

Free growing stand requirement applies to each hectare | Section 46.11

46.11   (1) Subject to subsection (2), a person who has an obligation to establish a free growing stand under

  1. section 29 of the Act in accordance with section 44 or 46.2 (5) of this regulation,

  2. Part 11 of the Act in accordance with section 69.1 or 70 of the Code, or

  3. section 46 (1) or 111 (4) of this regulation

must ensure that the obligation is fulfilled on each hectare within the net area to be reforested, unless otherwise specified in a forest stewardship plan.

Requirements if free growing stand cannot be established | Section 46.2

46.2   (1) Subject to section 108 of the Act and section 97.1 of this regulation, a person who

  1. is required to establish a free growing stand under sections 44 to 46 of this regulation, and

  2. knows that the requirements of sections 44 to 46 of this regulation, as applicable, cannot be met,

must

  1. give notice to the minister that the requirements to establish a free growing stand cannot be met, giving the reasons, and

  2. submit to the minister a proposal for establishing a free growing stand on the area, including the stocking standards, the free growing height and the latest date by which the stocking standards and free growing height will be achieved.

  1. The minister must approve a proposal submitted under subsection (1) if the minister considers that the proposal is consistent with section 26 (3).

  2. The minister must give notice to the person who submitted the proposal if the proposal has been approved or rejected and, if rejected, must provide written reasons.

  3. A rejection under subsection (3) is reviewable as set out in sections 80 and 81 of the Act and those sections and sections 82 to 84 of the Act apply in respect of the review.

  4. A person who is notified under subsection (3) that the proposal has been approved, must ensure that a free growing stand is established that conforms to the approved proposal.

Harvesting adjacent to another cutblock | Section 65

65   (1) In this section:

“adjacent” means an area that is sufficiently close to a cutblock that, due to its location, could directly impact on, or be impacted by, a forest practice carried out within the cutblock;

“existing cutblock” means a cutblock that was previously harvested under an agreement other than a minor tenure;

“new cutblock” means a cutblock on which harvesting has not yet started and that is adjacent to an existing cutblock;

“non-conforming portion” means an area within an existing cutblock on which the stocking and height requirements of subsection (3) have not been met.

  1. An agreement holder other than a holder of a minor tenure must not harvest timber on a new cutblock, unless

  1. all existing cutblocks that are adjacent to the new cutblock meet the requirements set out in subsection (3), or

  2. the combined area of the new cutblock and any non-conforming portions that are immediately adjacent to the new cutblock does not exceed the requirements relating to cutblock size set out in section 64 (1) [maximum cutblock size].

  1. For the purpose of subsection (2) (a), an existing cutblock must meet the criteria set out in one of the following paragraphs:

  1. at least 75% of the net area to be reforested of the existing cutblock is stocked such that the average height of the tallest 10% of the trees on the area is a minimum of 3 m and

  2. is stocked in accordance with the applicable stocking standards, as described under section 16 [stocking standards],

  1. if the area is on the Coast, other than the Nass timber supply area, is stocked with at least 500 trees/ha of a commercially valuable species that are at least 1.3 m in height, or

  2. if the area is in the Interior or in the Nass timber supply area, is stocked with at least 700 trees/ha of a commercially valuable species that are at least 1.3 m in height;

  1. the part of the net area to be reforested of the existing cutblock that is closest to the new cutblock

  2. must be at least half of the net area to be reforested,

  1. is stocked such that the average height of the tallest 10% of the trees on the area is a minimum of 3 m, and

  2. is stocked

  1. in accordance with the applicable stocking standards for that cutblock, as described under section 16,

  2. if the area is on the Coast, other than the Nass timber supply area, with at least 500 trees/ha of a commercially valuable species that are at least 1.3 m in height, or

  3. if the area is in the Interior or in the Nass timber supply area, with at least 700 trees/ha of a commercially valuable species that are at least 1.3 m in height.

  1. Subsection (2) does not apply if section 64 (2), (3) or (4) apply to the new cutblock.

Government assumption of obligation to establish free growing stand | Section 95

95   (1) In this section:

“affiliate” has the same meaning as “affiliate” in section 1 (1) of the Forest Act;

“associated with” means being associated with another person in a business activity whether by partnership, joint venture, contract or otherwise, and includes the contractual relationship between a licence holder and a person to whom the licence holder is contractually obliged to supply, directly or indirectly, some or all of the timber harvested under the licence holder’s agreement.

  1. For the purpose of section 30 (1) (d) [free growing stands for non-replaceable licences] of the Act, a “licence holder” means a person who

  1. does not hold a replaceable timber sale licence that has an allowable annual cut of greater than 10 000 m3, and

  1. a replaceable tree farm licence or forest licence, or

  2. a replaceable timber sale licence that has an allowable annual cut greater than 10 000 m3,

  1. is not affiliated with a corporation that holds shares of any type in

  1. a replaceable tree farm licence or forest licence, or

  2. a replaceable timber sale licence that has an allowable annual cut greater than 10 000 m3, and

  1. is not associated with a holder of

  1. a replaceable tree farm licence or forest licence, or

  2. a replaceable timber sale licence that has an allowable annual cut greater than 10 000 m3.

  1. For the purpose of section 30 (3) of the Act, the prescribed period for giving a notice under that section to a licence holder is one year.

  2. For the purpose of section 30 (3) (d) of the Act, the following requirements must be met before a district manager or timber sales manager may assume a licence holder’s responsibility for establishing a free growing stand:

  1. the licence holder requests that the district manager or timber sales manager, as applicable, assume responsibility for establishing a free growing stand on all cutblocks that are harvested under the licence holder’s agreement under the Forest Act, as and when the requirements referred to in section 30 (3) (a) to (c) of the Act are met in respect of those cutblocks;

  2. the request referred to in paragraph (a) is made by the licence holder as part of the licence holder’s first application under the Forest Act for a cutting permit for the agreement.
