Declarations | Section 84

84   (1) A woodlot licence holder may make a declaration under section 107 [limitation on liability of persons to government] of the Act that a free growing stand has been established on a cutblock at any time before the date referred to in section 34 [free growing stands] if the stand

  1. has met the free growing height that relates to the area, and

  2. is not under threat from

  3. competing plants, shrubs or other trees established on the area, or

  1. insects, disease or other factors adverse to forest health in the area.

Invasive Species and Disease | 8.4 Pathogens | Designation | 2 - Fish

  1. A person may make a declaration under section 107 [limitation on liability of persons to government] of the Act in respect of a cutblock referred to in section 35 (2) [conforming to stocking standards] no earlier than 12 months after the completion of harvesting on the area.

  2. A woodlot licence holder who makes a declaration under section 107 of the Act that the requirements for the regeneration date or free growing date on an area have been met must include with the declaration a forest cover inventory for the area to which the declaration applies.

  3. The prescribed period for giving a notice to a woodlot licence holder under section 107 (3) of the Act is 15 months.

Process respecting orders and exemptions | Section 86

86   (1) An order or exemption under this regulation must

  1. be in writing,

  2. specify the matter to which it relates,

  3. specify when the order or exemption comes into effect,

  4. be delivered to the woodlot licence holder to whom the order or exemption applies, and

  5. be filed with the district office for the forest district in which the area or thing to which the order or exemption applies is located.

  1. An order or exemption referred to in subsection (1) takes effect on the later of the date

  1. specified in the order or exemption, or

  2. the order or exemption is received by the woodlot licence holder to whom the order or exemption applies.

  1. For the purpose of subsection (2) (b), an order or exemption is received

  1. on the date it is delivered, if it is delivered in person to

  2. the woodlot licence holder to whom it applies or that holder’s representative, or

  1. the place of business of the woodlot licence holder to whom it applies,

  1. on the eighth day after it is mailed, if it is delivered by registered mail, or

  2. on the date referred to in a confirmation of delivery, if it is delivered electronically or by facsimile transmission.

Intervention orders | Section 88

88   (1) For the purpose of section 77 (1) [power of intervention: general] of the Act, an order given by the minister must specify

  1. the measures or actions that must be taken,

  2. the grounds for requiring the measures or actions to be taken, and

  3. whether or not the holder may recover all or part of the amount reasonably incurred in taking the specified measures or actions.

  1. The minister may act under section 77 (1) or (2) of the Act if the act or omission of the holder will likely result in

  1. a significant failure in meeting the stocking requirements described in section 35 [conforming to stocking standards],

  2. a significant delay in meeting the stocking requirements by the dates described in section 35, or

  3. a fundamental and adverse alteration of an ecosystem.

Administrative penalties | Section 89

89   For the purpose of section 71 (5) (g) [administrative penalties] of the Act, before levying an administrative penalty in respect of a contravention by a woodlot licence holder, the minister may

  1. request recommendations in respect of the contravention and penalty from any interested group, and

  2. if a request under paragraph (a) is made, act on any recommendation received from the group to which the request was made.

Classes of pesticides | Section 2

2   The following classes of pesticides are established:

  1. permit-restricted pesticides, being those pesticides assigned to this class under section 43 (1) [classification of pesticides] because the administrator considers that the risk of unreasonable adverse effects from their use should be evaluated for each proposed use;

  2. restricted pesticides, being those pesticides that

  3. are required under the federal Act to be labelled with the product class designation “RESTRICTED”, and

  1. are not permit-restricted pesticides or excluded pesticides;

  2. commercial pesticides, being those pesticides that

  3. are required under the federal Act to bear a label indicating their product class designation acceptable under that Act in relation to their general uses in commercial activities that are specified on the label as “commercial”, “industrial”, “agricultural” or another commercial activity, and

  4. are not permit-restricted pesticides or excluded pesticides;

  1. as a term of the new certificate, agrees to complete the difference between the number of continuing education credits accumulated in the 5 year period referred to in subparagraph (i) and 20 within the period specified for that purpose in the certificate.
  1. A continuing education credit is equal to one hour of training that is

  1. in relation to a matter set out in Schedule 3, and

  2. provided by a training provider that

  3. is approved by the administrator,

  1. provides training approved by the administrator, and

  2. maintains, for at least 5 years, registration, attendance and course completion information for each student.

Definitions | Section 1

“Act” means the Land Act;

and includes a pulpwood agreement;

“land use objective” means an objective

  1. established under section 93.4 of the Act, or

“minister” means the minister responsible for the administration of the Land Act;

“section 93.4 order” means an order made under section 93.4 of the Act for the purposes of the Forest and Range Practices Act.

Criteria for establishing land use objectives | Section 2

2   (1) In making a section 93.4 order establishing or significantly amending a land use objective for an area, the minister may consider information that

Spatial Designation | Interpretation & Purpose | 4 - Governance

  1. is contained in a land use plan that is endorsed by the Executive Council and that relates to the area, or

Spatial Designation | Designation | 4 - Governance

  1. is relevant to the management and use of the forest and range resources within the area.
  1. Before making a section 93.4 order establishing or significantly amending a land use objective, the minister must be satisfied that

Spatial Designation | Interpretation & Purpose | 4 - Governance

  1. the land use objective or amendment will

Spatial Designation | Interpretation & Purpose | 4 - Governance

  1. provide for management and use of forest or range resources in a manner that has not otherwise been provided for under this regulation or another enactment, and

  2. provide for an appropriate balance of social, economic and environmental benefits, and

Spatial Designation | 4 - Governance

  1. the importance of the land use objective or amendment outweighs any adverse impact on opportunities for timber harvesting or forage use within or adjacent to the area that will be affected.

Spatial Designation | Interpretation & Purpose | 4 - Governance

  1. In making a section 93.4 order establishing or significantly amending a land use objective the minister must consider any written comment received under whichever is applicable of section 3 or 4.

in accordance with subsection (2), or

1   One of the following vector attraction reduction processes is required for Class A biosolids or Class B biosolids used to produce biosolids growing medium:

  1. a digestion process (aerobic or anaerobic) resulting in the mass of volatile solids of the biosolids being reduced by more than 38 percent;

  2. when the 38 percent volatile solids reduction requirement in paragraph (a) cannot be met for an aerobically digested biosolids, vector attraction reduction can be demonstrated by digesting a portion of the previously digested biosolids that has a percent solids of two percent or less aerobically in the laboratory in a bench-scale unit for 30 additional days at 20° Celsius. When, at the end of the 30 days, the volatile solids in the biosolids at the beginning of that period is reduced by less than 15 percent, vector attraction reduction is achieved;

  3. when the 38 percent volatile solids reduction requirement in paragraph (a) cannot be met for an anaerobically digested biosolids, vector attraction reduction can be demonstrated by digesting a portion of the previously digested biosolids anaerobically in the laboratory in a bench-scale unit for 40 additional days at a temperature between 30° and 37° Celsius. When, at the end of the 40 days, the volatile solids in the biosolids at the beginning of that period is reduced by less than 17 percent, vector attraction reduction is achieved;

  4. the specific oxygen uptake rate (SOUR) for biosolids treated in an aerobic process shall be less than or equal to 1.5 milligrams of oxygen per hour per gram of total solids (dry weight basis) at a temperature of 20° Celsius;

  5. the pH of biosolids shall be raised to 12 or higher by alkali addition and, without the addition of more alkali, shall remain at 12 or higher for two hours and then at 11.5 or higher for an additional 22 hours;

  6. the percent solids of biosolids generated in a wastewater treatment process must be equal to or greater than 90 percent based on the moisture content and total solids prior to mixing with other materials. The biosolids must thereafter be managed in such a way that the moisture content of the biosolids does not increase such that compliance with the 90 percent solids requirement is maintained until such time as the biosolids is land applied in accordance with section 7 (2) or distributed in accordance with 7 (4) of this regulation.

1   Fecal coliform levels must be determined to be < 1 000 MPN per gram of total solids (dry weight basis) for

  1. the alkaline stabilization method consisting of maintaining the pH within the biosolids at above 12 for 72 hours with a temperature during the 72 hour period greater than 52° Celsius for 12 hours. 2   One of the following vector attraction reduction processes are required for Class A compost:

  1. Class A compost must be treated in an aerobic process for 14 days or longer. During that time, the temperature of the compost must be higher than 40° Celsius and the average temperature of the compost must be higher than 45° Celsius. After the vector attraction reduction process is completed the carbon to nitrogen ratio of the compost must be greater than or equal to 15:1 and less than or equal to 35:1;

  2. Class A compost must be retained in curing piles for at least 21 days. After the 21 day period, the carbon to nitrogen ratio of the Class A compost must be greater than or equal to 15:1 and less than or equal to 35:1 and must not re-heat, upon standing, under the following conditions:

  3. compost is aerated and formed into a pile no smaller than 3 metres in diameter and 2 metres high with compost having a moisture content between 35 percent and 60 percent;

  1. the pile must be formed in a location where the ambient temperature remains in the range of 5° to 30° Celsius;

  2. 3 days after the pile has been formed, the temperature of the compost is measured at a depth of 60 cm into the pile from the outside surface of the pile;

  3. the compost must not re-heat upon standing to greater than 20° Celsius above ambient temperature.

2   Determination of fecal coliform levels is not required for Class A compost produced from yard waste alone.

4   One of the following pathogen reduction processes specified in paragraphs (a) to (c) is required to produce Class A compost:

Invasive Species and Disease | 8.4 Pathogens | Designation | 2 - Fish

  1. the windrow composting method whereby organic matter is processed in a windrow involving periodic aeration and mixing of the windrow, with a temperature of not less than 55° Celsius maintained for at least 15 days and not fewer than 5 turnings of the windrow made during the high temperature period to promote uniform exposure of the compost to thermophilic temperatures;

  2. the static aerated pile composting method consisting of a compost process involving mechanical aeration of the compost pile, with the compost pile insulated and a temperature of not less than 55° Celsius maintained throughout the compost pile for at least 3 consecutive days;

  3. the enclosed vessel method consisting of a confined compost process involving mechanical aeration of compost under controlled environmental conditions, with a temperature of not less than 55° Celsius maintained for at least 3 days during the composting process.

Transition — matters in progress | Section 7

7   For Class B biosolids and Class B compost a biosolids treatment or composting process must be used whereby fecal coliform are reduced to levels < 2 000 000 MPN per gram of total solids (dry weight basis), or one of the following processes must be used:

  1. the aerobic digestion process whereby Class B biosolids are agitated with air or oxygen to maintain aerobic conditions for a specific mean cell residence time at a specific temperature. Values for the mean cell residence time and temperature must be between 40 days at 20° Celsius and 60 days at 15° Celsius;

  2. the air-drying process whereby Class B biosolids are dried on sand beds or on paved or unpaved basins. The biosolids must dry for a minimum of 3 months. During 2 of the 3 months, the ambient average daily temperature must be above 0° Celsius;

  3. the anaerobic digestion process whereby Class B biosolids are treated in the absence of air for a specific mean cell residence time at a specific temperature. Values for the mean cell time and temperature must be between 15 days at 35° Celsius to 55° Celsius and 60 days at 20° Celsius;

  4. the compost process using either within-vessel, static aerated pile or windrow-composting methods whereby the temperature of the Class B compost is raised to 40° Celsius or higher and maintained for 5 days. For 4 hours during the 5-day period, the temperature in the compost pile must exceed 55° Celsius;

  5. the lime stabilization process whereby sufficient lime is added to the Class B biosolids to raise the pH of the biosolids to 12 after 2 hours of contact.

  1. all compost must be applied or distributed in accordance with this regulation, and

  4. under section 6 (3) of the Public Notification Regulation, publish the application, or

  5. under section 6 (5) of the Public Notification Regulation, post the application in a post office.

  1. Section 2 (2) does not apply to a discharger described in subsection (1) until the requirement is met if the discharger fails to

  2. meet a requirement under the Public Notification Regulation by the time specified in that regulation.

  1. A discharger to which subsection (1) applies is exempt from section 3.1 (1) until the date the director makes a decision in relation to the discharger’s application under subsection (1) of this section.

Reforestation of areas where timber harvested or destroyed | Section 31

31   (1) In this section:

“completion of timber harvesting” means the date that timber harvesting within a cutblock is concluded and is determined by

  1. the date the area is declared as a cutblock in an annual declaration, or

  2. if an area is not included in a declaration, a date that does not exceed two consecutive operating seasons from the commencement of harvesting in the cutblock;

“crop tree” means a tree that

  1. is of a commercial species that is consistent with the species of trees specified in the management commitment for use in reforestation, and

  2. is unencumbered by pathogens;

Invasive Species and Disease | 8.4 Pathogens | 2 - Fish

“disturbed area” means all or part of private managed forest land where

  1. timber harvesting has been completed within a cutblock, or

  2. timber was destroyed

but does not include an area occupied by roads referred to in section 13 or logging trails referred to in section 14 (1);

Forest and Range | 5.3 Logging, Harvesting & Controlling Trees | Designation | 3 - Habitat

“restock” means to establish a stand of trees that contains at least

  1. 400 crop trees per hectare reasonably well distributed across the disturbed area if the stand is on the Coast, and

  2. 600 crop trees per hectare reasonably well distributed across the disturbed area if the stand is in the Interior;

“successfully regenerated stand” means a stand of trees

  1. that contains at least

  2. 400 crop trees per hectare reasonably well distributed across the disturbed area if the stand is on the Coast, and

  1. 600 crop trees per hectare reasonably well distributed across the disturbed area if the stand is in the Interior, and

  1. where the crop trees exceed the height of competing vegetation within 1 m of the crop tree by

  2. 50% if the area is on the Coast, and

  1. 25% if the area is in the Interior.
  1. This section does not apply to an owner of a disturbed area if

  1. the area where the timber was harvested or destroyed is a contiguous area that is under 1 ha in size, or

  2. the trees remaining on the area meet the definition of a successfully regenerated stand.

  1. If all or part of private managed forest land becomes a disturbed area, an owner or a contractor, employee or agent of the owner must reforest the disturbed area by

  1. restocking the disturbed area within 5 years of the completion of timber harvesting activity on the cutblock, or the date the timber was destroyed, as applicable, and

  2. establishing a successfully regenerated stand on the disturbed area within 15 years of the completion of timber harvesting activity on the cutblock, or the date the timber was destroyed, as applicable.

  1. Nothing in this section requires an owner to reforest a disturbed area if the timber on the area was

  1. destroyed and the disturbed area is not sufficiently productive to support a successfully regenerated stand, or

  2. harvested or destroyed and the disturbed area becomes occupied by buildings or other structures or installations.

[am. B.C. Reg. 539/2004.]

Exit fees | Section 2

2   (1) Subject to section 45 (2) of the Act and section 3 (1), if the assessor declassifies managed forest land under section 24 (3) (b) of the Assessment Act, the council must

  1. determine, in accordance with subsection (2), the amount of the exit fee that the owner of the land is required to pay under section 19 (1) of the Act, and

  2. notify the owner of the amount of the exit fee.

  1. For the purpose of subsection (3) the assessor may determine the total annual property tax that would have been due for the property that is being removed from the managed forest land class, had that property not been valued and classified as managed forest land for the immediately preceding tax year roll, less the total property tax that was payable for the immediately preceding tax year on the property that is being removed from the managed forest land class.

  2. The exit fee referred to in subsection (1) is the amount determined by finding the product of the following:

Total annual property tax as determined under subsection (2)

Multiplied by

Number of consecutive years ending in the current tax year that the property has been classified as managed forest land

Multiplied by

Adjustment Factor noted in Schedule B for the number of years classified as managed forest land for assessment purposes.

  1. If the estimated total annual property taxes for the property for the immediately preceding tax year based on reclassification out of the managed forest land class is less than the total annual property taxes payable for the property in the managed forest land class for the immediately preceding tax year, no exit fee is payable.

  2. If the property has been classified managed forest land for 15 or more years, no exit fee is payable.

  3. In determining the number of years a property was classified as managed forest land for the purposes of the calculation under subsection (3), the time the property was classified as managed forest land before the coming into force of this section will be included.

Exemption from exit fees | Section 3

3   (1) For the purpose of section 19 (1) of the Act, the circumstances in which an owner is not required to pay an exit fee in respect of a portion of land that has been declassified under section 24 (3) of the Assessment Act are that the portion of land

  1. is subject to a right of way or easement,

  2. is expropriated,

  3. is gifted to the government or local government, or

  4. is subject to a land exchange with the government or local government.

  1. Despite subsection (1), if land is declassified as a result of notification to the assessor under section 31 (1) of the Act, the owner must pay the exit fee calculated under section 2.

Offences for contravening this regulation | Section 11

11   (1) A person who contravenes section 5 (2) commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding $50 000.

  1. A person who contravenes section 6 (2) commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding $25.

  2. A person who contravenes section 8 (2) commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding

  1. $1 000 for a first offence, and

  2. $5 000 for a second or any subsequent offence.

8   A person may apply in writing to the district manager for a special use permit if the person

Issuance of special use permit | Section 9

9   (1) Subject to subsection (2), the district manager may issue a special use permit if

  1. the applicant

  2. has applied in accordance with section 8, and

  1. submitted a plan that sets out how the land will be used, and

  1. the district manager is of the opinion that

  2. the issuance of the special use permit would not impair the proper management and conservation of forest resources on Crown land, and

  1. any activity under the special use permit will not impair the ability of any affected holder of an agreement under the Forest Act or Range Act to exercise its rights or fulfill its obligations under the agreement.
  1. The district manager may issue the special use permit subject to

  1. a condition that the holder of the permit carry out the activity in accordance with the plan submitted under subsection (1),

  2. any conditions the district manager determines necessary to conserve forest resources and the natural environment, including a condition

  1. restricting, regulating and prohibiting the building of or disposal of any chattel or fixture, and

  2. a condition that the holder provide, in an amount specified in the permit, a deposit in the form of money or other securities acceptable to the district manager

  3. to ensure the conditions of the permit are met, or

  4. if personal property owned by a person other than the holder or the government is situated on the land under the permit.

(2.01) The holder of a special use permit must comply with the conditions of the permit, if any.

(2.1) In issuing a special use permit, the district manager must specify its term, which must not exceed the following:

  1. 4 years, if the special use permit is issued for a purpose set out in section 7 (1.1) (d) or (g);

  2. 5 years, if the special use permit is issued for a purpose set out in section 7 (1.1) (e), (f), (i), (j) (i) or (k) or (1.2) (b) or (c);

  3. 10 years, if the special use permit is issued for a purpose set out in section 7 (1.1) (a), (b), (c), (h) or (j) (ii) or (1.2) (a).

  1. The district manager may use any or all of the deposit referred to in subsection (2) (c)

  1. to satisfy a claim made by the owner of the personal property referred to in subsection (2) (c) (ii),

  2. to cover the costs resulting from a failure of the holder to meet the conditions of the permit or

  3. to cover the costs resulting from a failure of the holder to comply with an order under section 15 (1) (a) or (b).

  1. No later than 12 months after the date the special use permit expires or is cancelled, the remainder of the deposit must be returned to the holder of the permit.

  1. The holder of a special use permit must pay the annual charge described in subsection (1) no later than,

  1. for the first year of the special use permit, 60 days after the date the permit is issued, and

  2. for all subsequent years, 60 days after the date an invoice is issued for the annual charge.

Assignment prohibited | Section 10

10   A holder of a special use permit must not assign the special use permit to another person without the consent of the district manager.

No exclusive rights to the use of the land | Section 11

11   Rights granted under a special use permit are not exclusive and do not prevent the government from using the land or authorizing others to use the land in accordance with the Act or this regulation.

Permit extension | Section 12

12   (1) On application by the holder no less than 6 months before the expiry of a special use permit, the district manager may grant an extension of the term of the permit specified under section 9 (2.1) if the district manager is satisfied of all of the following:

  1. the holder continues to hold a licence, agreement, permit or authorization to which the special use permit relates;

  2. the holder has begun to exercise the rights granted under the special use permit;

  3. the holder has performed the conditions of the special use permit;

  4. the holder has paid all deposits and charges in relation to the special use permit;

  5. the special use permit is not suspended at the time of application;

  6. the conditions set out in section 9 (2) (b) will continue to be met;

  7. the application demonstrates that an extension is necessary.

  1. An extension under subsection (1)

  1. may be granted once for a term not exceeding 2 years if the special use permit was issued for a purpose set out in section 7 (1.1) (d) or (g),

  2. may be granted twice for terms not exceeding 5 years each if the special use permit was issued for a purpose set out in section 7 (1.1) (e), (f), (i), (j) (i) or (k) or (1.2) (b) or (c), and

  3. may be granted for terms not exceeding 10 years each if the special use permit was issued for a purpose set out in section 7 (1.1) (a), (b) (c), (h) or (j)  (ii) or (1.2) (a).

  1. If the maximum number of extensions described in subsection (2) (a) or (b) has been granted, the district manager may issue a replacement special use permit if the district manager is satisfied that the Crown land may not be managed or used under a tenure under the Land Act for the purpose authorized in the special use permit.

  2. When granting an extension under subsection (1), the district manager may do one or both of the following:

  1. require that the holder submit an updated plan described in section 9 (1) (a) (ii);

  2. amend any of the conditions described in section 9 (2).

  1. If the district manager does not make a decision under subsection (1) before the expiry of the special use permit, the holder may continue to manage or use Crown land under the permit until a decision is made.

[en. B.C. Reg. 57/2024, Sch. 3, s. 6.]

Cancellation and suspension | Section 13

13   (1) Subject to subsection (2), sections 76, 76.1 and 77 of the Forest Act, except section 77 (5), apply to the cancellation or suspension of a special use permit under this section.

(1.1) The district manager may suspend or cancel a special use permit if any of the following applies:

  1. the holder of the special use permit

  2. has failed to provide a deposit described in section 9 (2) (c) or to pay the annual charge under section 9.1 by the required date, and

  1. the deposit or annual charge has been in arrears for more than 6 months;

  1. the holder of the special use permit has failed to comply with an order under section 15 (1);

  2. 2 years after the date the permit is issued, the holder of the special use permit has not begun to exercise the rights granted under the special use permit;

  3. the district manager

  4. has, for more than 6 months, not been able to locate or contact the holder of the special use permit, or

  1. is satisfied that the holder of the special use permit no longer exists;

  1. the district manager is satisfied that the holder of the special use permit is insolvent because the holder

  2. has filed for protection under the Companies’ Creditors Arrangement Act (Canada), or

  1. is a bankrupt or insolvent person under the Bankruptcy and Insolvency Act (Canada).
  1. The district manager may cancel a special use permit without notice and without suspending the permit prior to cancellation if the holder contravenes section 10.

[am. B.C. Regs. 347/97, s. 6; 57/2024, Sch. 3, s. 7; 223/2024, s. 2.]

Holder’s obligations on permit expiry, surrender, suspension or cancellation | Section 14

14   On the expiry, surrender, suspension or cancellation of a special use permit, the holder or former holder of the special use permit must do all of the following:

  1. pay any outstanding charge or deposit the holder owes the government in respect of the special use permit;

  2. fulfill any outstanding obligation of the holder or former holder under the special use permit;

  3. fulfill any outstanding obligation of the holder or former holder under the Act, the Forest and Range Practices Act, the Wildfire Act or any other enactment, in respect of any of the holder’s activities under the special use permit.

[en. B.C. Reg. 57/2024, Sch. 3, s. 8.]

Deactivation and remediation orders | Section 15

15   (1) The minister may, by order, require the holder or former holder of a special use permit, including a special use permit that has expired or is surrendered, suspended or cancelled, to do one or both of the following:

  1. deactivate a road authorized in the special use permit;

  2. remediate the land that is the subject of the special use permit.

  1. An order under this section must include the following:

  1. a description of the location of the road to be deactivated or of the land to be remediated;

  2. the date by which the deactivation or remediation must be completed.

  1. A holder or former holder of a special use permit who receives an order under this section must comply with the order.

[en. B.C. Reg. 57/2024, Sch. 3, s. 8.]

Entry on Crown land | Section 16

16   (1) Subject to subsection (2), the holder or former holder of a special use permit may enter onto Crown land for the purpose of fulfilling any of the obligations described in section 14 (b) and (c) or complying with an order under section 15 (1).

  1. The district manager may impose on the holder or former holder of a special use permit who enters onto Crown land for a purpose described in subsection (1) any condition that the minister considers necessary or desirable.

  2. A holder or former holder of a special use permit must comply with any conditions imposed by the minister under subsection (2).

[en. B.C. Reg. 57/2024, Sch. 3, s. 8; am. B.C. Regs. 62/2024, Sch., s. 47; 223/2024, s. 3.]

Existing special use permits | Section 17

17   Sections 9.1, 9.2, 13 (1.1) and 14 to 16 apply to a special use permit issued before the date this Part comes into force.

[en. B.C. Reg. 57/2024, Sch. 3, s. 9.]

Transition — annual charge | Section 18

18   The annual charge for a special use permit issued before the date this Part comes into force is, during the first year after the date this Part comes into force, the greater of

  1. half of the annual charge determined in accordance with section 9.2 (3) (b), and

  2. whichever of the following that applies:

  3. for a special use permit issued for a purpose set out in section 7 (1.1) (a), (b), (c), (d), (e), (f), (g) or (k), $675;

  1. for a special use permit issued for a purpose set out in section 7 (1.1) (h), (i) or (j), $500.

[en. B.C. Reg. 57/2024, Sch. 3, s. 9.]

Transition — replacement permit | Section 19

19   (1) On the expiry of a special use permit issued before the date this Part comes into force for any purpose set out in section 7 (1.1) or (1.2), except a purpose set out in section 7 (1.1) (d) or (g), the district manager may issue a replacement permit under section 12, as it read immediately before the date this Part comes into force, if, in addition to the matters set out in section 12, the district manager is satisfied of all of the following:

  1. the holder continues to hold a licence, agreement, permit or authorization to which the special use permit relates;

  2. the holder has begun to exercise the rights granted under the special use permit;

  3. the holder has paid all deposits and charges in relation to the special use permit;

  4. the special use permit is not suspended at the time of application;

  5. the holder has demonstrated that a replacement permit is necessary.

  1. The district manager may issue only one replacement permit for each special use permit.

[en. B.C. Reg. 57/2024, Sch. 3, s. 9.]

Transition — permit extension | Section 20

20   (1) This section applies to a special use permit issued before the coming into force of this Part

  1. for a purpose set out in section 7 (1.1) (d) or (g),

  2. for a purpose other than a purpose set out in section 7, or

  3. to a person who does not hold a licence, agreement, permit or authorization to which the special use permit relates.

  1. A special use permit that expires before the date that is one year after the date this Part comes into force is extended for a term of one year from the date the special use permit expires.

  2. If, before the expiry of the term referred to in subsection (2), the permit holder submits to the district manager proof of the holder’s application for a licence, agreement, permit or authorization that would authorize the purpose for the special use permit, the district manager may grant an extension of the term of the special use permit

  1. for up to 2 years, or

  2. for up to 4 years if the district manager is satisfied that special circumstances exist.

  1. If, before the expiry of a special use permit, the permit holder submits to the district manager proof of the holder’s application, made no less than 6 months before the expiry of the special use permit, for tenure under another enactment that would authorize the purpose for the special use permit, the district manager may grant an extension of the term of the special use permit

  1. for up to 2 years, or

  2. for up to 4 years if the district manager is satisfied that special circumstances exist.

  1. An extension granted under subsection (3) or (4) must include a condition that the permit holder notify the district manager of the decision made on the application for tenure under another enactment as soon as practicable after the permit holder is notified of the decision.

  2. Once the district manager receives notification under subsection (5) that tenure has been granted to the permit holder, the district manager may cancel the special use permit whose term was extended under this section.

[en. B.C. Reg. 57/2024, Sch. 3, s. 9.]

“mine” has the same meaning as in the Mines Act;

“mineral mine” means a mine where a mineral, as defined in the Mineral Tenure Act, is or could be mined, but does not include a mine where industrial minerals are or could be mined;

“offshore mine” means a platform, artificial island or other physical work or structure, including any associated facilities, that is intended to be used, or is used, for the exploration for or production of a minable substance from the foreshore or submerged land along a marine coastline, or from an offshore site located in salt water;

“pay dirt” means mined placer gravel that is or could be processed in a sluice box, wash plant or other device for extracting precious metals;

“permitted for disturbance” in relation to land, means that the land would be or has been disturbed by mining activities approved under a Mines Act permit or another permit that was issued as part of a previous mine approval;

“placer mineral mine” means a mine where a placer mineral, as defined in the Mineral Tenure Act, is or could be mined;

“production capacity”, in relation to a mine project, means a capacity to generate product for marketing or testing, not including waste materials;

Pollution | 9.1 Water-Borne & Other Effluent Pollution | Interpretation & Purpose | 3 - Habitat

“proposed project”, in relation to the proposed modification of the existing facility referred to in section 10 (1) or (2), means all of the physical works and structures of the existing facility together with all of the physical works and structures that would be constructed as part of the proposed modification;

“quarry” means a quarry or other operation where construction stone, an industrial mineral or another substance is or could be mined, but does not include a mineral mine, placer mineral mine or coal mine or a sand or gravel pit;

“raw coal” means coal that does not require processing in a coal preparation plant before it is transported from the mine site for marketing or testing;

“threshold E” means the criteria described in section 10 (1);

“threshold F” means the criteria described in section 10 (2);

“threshold G” means the criteria described in section 10 (3).

Criteria for proposed modifications of mine projects | Section 10

10   (1) For the purposes of this Part, threshold E is met for a proposed modification of an existing project if

  1. the existing project, or the proposed project, were it a new project in the same category as the existing project as described in Column 1 of the applicable table, would meet the criteria set out opposite in Column 2, and

  2. the modification will result in the disturbance of an area of land that was not previously permitted for disturbance and that is at least 50% of the area of land that was previously permitted for disturbance at the existing project.

  1. In this Part, threshold F is met for a proposed modification of an existing project if

  1. the existing project, or the proposed project, were it a new project in the same category as the existing project as described in Column 1 of the applicable table, would meet the criteria set out opposite in Column 2, and

  2. the modification will result in the disturbance of an area of land that was not previously permitted for disturbance and that is at least 35% of the area of land that was previously permitted for disturbance at the existing project.

  1. In this Part, threshold G is met for a proposed modification of an existing project if

  1. the existing project, or the proposed project, were it a new project in the same category as the existing project as described in Column 1 of the applicable table, would meet the criteria set out opposite in Column 2, and

  2. the chief executive assessment officer has determined under subsection (4) that the modification has the potential to result in a significant adverse environmental, economic, social, cultural or health effect.

Spatial Designation | 4 - Governance

  1. For the purposes of a modification of an existing project in the offshore mine project category, the chief executive assessment officer must determine whether the modification has the potential to result in a significant adverse environmental, economic, social, cultural or health effect.

Spatial Designation | Authorization & Mandate | 4 - Governance

  1. On receiving an assessment report under subsection (1), the minister may

  1. provide a copy of the report to a local government, or

  1. The minister may reject an assessment report under subsection (2) (b) if the minister considers that

  1. the assessment that is the subject of the report was not carried out in accordance with section 12 [assessments], or

  2. the report was not prepared in accordance with section 14 [assessment reports] or is not complete.

  1. For certainty, nothing in this section requires the minister to review a report that the minister does not reject.

  1. links aquatic to terrestrial ecosystems, and

  2. is capable of supporting streamside vegetation, and

Water Use and Watercourse Modifications | 7.2 Dams & Water Management / Use | 3 - Habitat

  1. in the case of a simple assessment, extends far enough upland from the stream that development outside the streamside protection and enhancement area will not result in any harmful alteration, disruption or destruction of natural features, functions and conditions in the area referred to in paragraph (a) that support the life processes of protected fish.

Water Use and Watercourse Modifications | 7.2 Dams & Water Management / Use | Designation | 3 - Habitat

  1. Without limiting subsection (1) (a) (ii), an area of human disturbance must be considered to be capable of supporting streamside vegetation if the area would be capable of supporting streamside vegetation were the area in a natural condition.

Water Use and Watercourse Modifications | 7.2 Dams & Water Management / Use | Instruction | 3 - Habitat

Riparian protection standard | Section 10

10   (1) Subject to subsections (2) to (4), a proposed development meets the riparian protection standard if the development

Water Use and Watercourse Modifications | 7.2 Dams & Water Management / Use | 3 - Habitat

  1. will not occur in the streamside protection and enhancement area, and

Water Use and Watercourse Modifications | 7.2 Dams & Water Management / Use | Designation | 3 - Habitat

  1. in the case of a detailed assessment, will not result in any harmful alteration, disruption or destruction of natural features, functions and conditions in the streamside protection and enhancement area that support the life processes of protected fish.

Water Use and Watercourse Modifications | 7.2 Dams & Water Management / Use | Designation | 3 - Habitat

  1. Subject to subsections (3) and (4), a proposed development on a site that is subject to undue hardship meets the riparian protection standard if

Water Use and Watercourse Modifications | 7.2 Dams & Water Management / Use | 3 - Habitat

  1. the development

  2. will not occur in the streamside protection and enhancement area, other than in a part of that area that is already an area of human disturbance,

Water Use and Watercourse Modifications | 7.2 Dams & Water Management / Use | Designation | 3 - Habitat

  1. will be situated and otherwise designed so as to minimize any encroachment into the streamside protection and enhancement area, and

Water Use and Watercourse Modifications | 7.2 Dams & Water Management / Use | Designation | 3 - Habitat

  1. in the case of a detailed assessment, will not result in any harmful alteration, disruption or destruction of natural features, functions and conditions in the streamside protection and enhancement area that support the life processes of protected fish, and

Water Use and Watercourse Modifications | 7.2 Dams & Water Management / Use | Designation | 3 - Habitat

  1. the areas of human disturbance on the site after the development is complete will not exceed the allowable footprint for the site.
  1. Subsections (1) and (2) (a) do not require

  1. a building or other structure that exists before the development occurs to be removed, if the structure will remain on its existing foundation and within its existing footprint, or

  2. any other area of human disturbance that exists before the development occurs to be returned or allowed to return to a natural condition, if the area will not be extended and the type of the disturbance will not be changed.

  1. A proposed development that involves a subdivision of a parcel or strata lot does not meet the riparian protection standard if the subdivision would create

Water Use and Watercourse Modifications | 7.2 Dams & Water Management / Use | 3 - Habitat

  1. a parcel that has a developable area that is less than the allowable footprint for that parcel, or

  2. a strata lot that has a developable area that is less than the allowable footprint for that strata lot.

Undue hardship | Section 11

11   (1) In this section, “variance” means any of the following:

  1. a variance that a board of variance may order to be permitted under section 542 [board powers on application] of the Local Government Act;

  2. a variance that a local government may permit under section 498 [development variance permits] of the Local Government Act;

  3. an amendment to a zoning bylaw.

  1. A site is subject to undue hardship for the purposes of this regulation if

  1. the site was created by subdivision in accordance with the laws in force in British Columbia at the time the site was created,

  2. the developer has sought and received a decision on every variance that would reduce the legally restricted area of the site, and

  3. the developable area of the site is less than the allowable footprint for the site.

  1. The allowable footprint for a site subject to undue hardship is the following:

  1. if the area of human disturbance on the site is less than or equal to 70% of the area of the site, the allowable footprint is 30% of the area of the site;

  2. if the area of human disturbance on the site is greater than 70% of the area of the site, the allowable footprint is 40%.

Assessments | Section 12

12   An assessment of a proposed development for the purposes of this regulation must be carried out

  1. by one or more qualified environmental professionals, and

Spatial Designation | 4 - Governance

  1. in accordance with

  2. section 13, and

  1. the technical manuals.

Simple and detailed assessments | Section 13

13   An assessment must determine the streamside protection and enhancement area for a stream, in accordance with the technical manuals, using one of the following methods:

Water Use and Watercourse Modifications | 7.2 Dams & Water Management / Use | Instruction | 3 - Habitat

  1. a method based on measurement from the stream boundary or, if the stream is in a ravine, from the top of the ravine bank;

Water Use and Watercourse Modifications | 7.2 Dams & Water Management / Use | Designation | 3 - Habitat

  1. a method based on the location of natural features, functions and conditions that support the life processes of protected fish.

Spatial Designation | 4 - Governance

  2. sections 15 to 19, and

  1. the technical manuals.

15   (1) An assessment report must include

  2. a description of the results of the assessment.

  1. A description under subsection (1) (b) must identify, in accordance with the technical manuals,
  1. the riparian assessment area,

Water Use and Watercourse Modifications | 7.2 Dams & Water Management / Use | Designation | 3 - Habitat

  1. the streamside protection and enhancement area, and

Water Use and Watercourse Modifications | 7.2 Dams & Water Management / Use | Designation | 3 - Habitat

Water Use and Watercourse Modifications | 7.2 Dams & Water Management / Use | Designation | 3 - Habitat

Recommended measures | Section 16

16   For each potential hazard identified under section 15 (2) (c), if applicable, an assessment report must

  1. explain how the design of the proposed development will avoid the hazard, or

  2. recommend measures to be taken to avoid the hazard.

Opinion on development | Section 17
